title: TechDocs - Documentation as catalog entities
description:
Currently, you can ingest markdown documents into Port by creating markdown properties. Each document will be displayed in Port as a tab on the specific entity page.

We would like to add the ability to create a "documentation tree" for each entity, allowing you to create a full wiki inside your developer portal.

Similar to the singular markdown documents, the documents in the "documentation tree" will be searchable via the [global search](https://roadmap.getport.io/ideas/p/global-search).

title: Categorizing Self Service actions
description: Allow categorizing self service actions for ease of finding appropriate actions for your needs.

title: Multi-step workflows
description: Chain multiple inputs, approvals, conditions, and actions via automatic triggers or self-service

title: SIEM Integration for Port's Audit log
description:
Some customers would like the option to automatically report Port's information to an external SIEM system for security concern. 

https://www.ibm.com/topics/siem#:~:text=Security%20information%20and%20event%20management,chance%20to%20disrupt%20business%20operations.

First and most important are the changes of Port's audit log

title: Ability to retry the action from the run page
description:
In some cases an operation failed and a retry will solve it.

Adding a retry action for a run can be nice addition :)

title: Audit log filter beyond the last 1,000 records
description:
Right now, the audit log only shows the latest 1000 records, and filtering applies only within those 1000. We’re planning to add an API route so that when a user filters, the frontend will send the filter to the backend, which will search across the entire audit log - not just the last 1000 entries.

The result will still show up to 1000 entries, but filtered from the full log. So for example, if a user filters by “fails,” they’ll get the latest 1000 fails overall, rather than fails just within the latest 1000 records.

title: Multi-select delete
description: Having to delete more than 10 entries on a page is TEDIOUS.  I would love to multi-select and delete an entire group or groups at once or at least all of the resources on the page at once.

title: Improved customizations of user inputs validations
description:
Port self-service actions already support a rich set of input controls: required fields, type enforcement, regex patterns, and JQ-powered dynamic forms. We want to take that further by letting portal builders define validation rules that run directly in the form, before execution.

This means conditional logic like "replica count must be at least 3 when deploying to production", cross-field rules like email confirmation, and meaningful error messages that actually tell users what to fix. All without touching backend scripts or waiting for a failed action run.

title: Microsoft teams notification
description:
Currently, the message sender only supports slack.

Some organizations use Microsoft teams, which means they cannot create notifications for their teams.

title: Steps in Port Self-Service Action Form
description:
As a developer using Port's self-service action form,

I want the ability to collapse the form into distinct sections such as network configuration, security configuration, and IAM role,

So that I can more easily navigate and digest the information, focusing on specific areas as needed based on my answers.

title: Improved UI for managing dynamic permissions
description:
Managing dynamic permissions requires specific skills and is more challenging to debug and verify.

To assist, we want to provide an improved UI that will allow us to test the result and verify users defined the permissions as expected.

title: Discussions & Comments on entities
description:
Ask questions, discuss, and make decisions within context. 

Allow developers to discuss and comment on different entities directly in Port.

title: More RBAC for admin permissions
description:
I would like more control over what permissions admins can have within the IDP.

For example, some admins can only edit automations, and webhooks, some admins can only edit the data model, or no admins can generate a new org token.

This enables following of least privilege principle.

The "superadmin" role could do anything.

Usecase: Our team is building a pipeline to version control data model changes as JSON, it would be nice if no one can update the data model through UI in our production environment anymore and they can only do it through the pipeline.

title: Specific Resync
description: Add option to specifically resync a predefined list of resources & do a scheduled resync only for a selected list of resources

title: Dropdown input based on API
description:
Currently, there is no way to offer input selection based on API.

Implementing this could allow forms for specific services based on their API responses.

For example, create a dropdown selection of Github organizations based on an API call.

title: JQ in Scorecard rules
description: Currently scorecard rules are defined by conditions that use the search/query system but these can get complicated for complex rules. It would be very useful if you could directly use JQ in these conditions.

title: Mirror properties from the other direction of relation
description: Add the ability to mirror a property from a related blueprint even, regardless of the direction of the relation.

title: Pause/cancel/resume data source sync
description: We need the ability to pause and resume data source syncs. While we understand that rate limits determine the sync frequency, having the option to pause and resume would give us control over the order in which data sources sync. This capability is essential as we gradually roll out Port to different teams, ensuring their service data is accurately captured and reviewed before proceeding to the next team.

title: Self-Service Action Approval Notifications
description: There is no option to automatically notify users when their requested actions have been approved. This feature request proposes adding an option that will send an email and/or Slack message to users once their self-service actions have been approved.

title: Better Error Messages for Denied Dynamic Permissions
description:
When a self service action is unable to be executed due to the dynamic permissions not allowing the execution, the error message logged provides no context about what specific part of the dynamic permission caused the action to be denied.

This makes troubleshooting and building permissions incredibly difficult as you have no idea what part of the permissions policy/condition caused the error.

The error message should explain what aspect of the policy's query/condition caused the rejection of the execution.

title: Support hiding/displaying self-service actions using dynamic permissions
description:
Currently, using the [dynamic permissions](https://docs.port.io/actions-and-automations/create-self-service-experiences/set-self-service-actions-rbac/dynamic-permissions) feature, self-service actions will still appear in the UI. In case the user is not permitted, the run will be rejected only after sending the self-service action form. 

As part of this item, we would like to support hiding/displaying self-service actions using the dynamic permissions policies.

title: Support for entities create, update, and delete dynamic permission policies
description: As described [here](https://docs.port.io/build-your-software-catalog/set-catalog-rbac/), the "policy" key for entity permissions is currently supported for the "read" permission type. As part of this item, we would like to add support for create, update, and delete operations as well.

title: Self-service actions - controlling the payload
description: Use JQ to manipulate the payload before sending it to the relevant workflow (Webhook, Kafka, GitHub Workflow, and any other invocation method)

title: Automation
description:
Currently, Port can trigger workflows when a change is made in the software catalog, for example, trigger a webhook. This is done with the [changelog listener](https://docs.getport.io/create-self-service-experiences/setup-backend/webhook/examples/changelog-listener). The main problem with the changelog listener is that only one trigger per blueprint can be defined, and each trigger is executed for any change in the catalog, without the ability to define rules for a specific trigger.

With the "Automations" feature, we plan to improve the changelog listener with the following capabilities:

1. The ability to create rules that need to pass in order to trigger automation.

2. Create multiple automations on a specific blueprint

3. Adding many more invocation types when triggering automation, such as executing a Port action, executing a CICD pipeline, and updating entities in the catalog

This will enable scenarios such as:

1. Sending a Slack message when the "Production readiness" scorecards changed from "Gold" to "Silver"

2. Scaling a Cluster according to changes in the CPU usage

3. Updating the "state" property of a service from "Healthy" to "Unhealthy" when a related incident opened in PagerDuty

Of course, these are just examples. The power of this capability is that each organization will be able to create automations based on their developer portal data and needs.

title: Support multiple event triggers in Automations
description:
Currently, it's only possible to configure an automation to be triggered on one specific event. For example, when an entity is created or when it gets updated.

As developers, building workflow automations, we would like the ability to configure a single automation to be triggered on multiple entity events, allowing us to manage fewer automation resources and avoid  code repetition.

title: Improve pages API routes
description: As for now the API route for pages and Sidebars are very complex (and it's still in beta), we need to have a better implementation for it

title: Associate action with multiple blueprints
description:
Currently as it stands, an action can only be associated with one blueprint. It would be great to have an action be associated with multiple blueprints, for example if we want to restart a service, all catalogs will have service overview and likely this action will be associated with service overview entity. In all scenarios there will also be services from respective container orchestration (ECS/EKS) - right now as it stands an action if associated with service overview entity cant be associated with the service blueprint entity - which means a new actions should be created which can be associated with the service (orchestration layer service). 

The goal here is to be able to use the lightning button and trigger actions instead of going to the action section and triggering it.

title: Support Input Secrets with Approvals in Self Service Actions
description:
Currently defining an input as a secret does not work in cases where there is an approver on the action. 

https://docs.getport.io/actions-and-automations/create-self-service-experiences/setup-ui-for-action/user-inputs/secret

Port should support using input secrets and approvers in the same action.

title: Self Service Action Workflow
description:
Add support for invoking multiple triggers in an action while allowing for an Approval to be added between triggers. 

For example:

Have an action triggering a webhook, github, gitlab action. Based on that first trigger result, prompt an approval request and based on the approval, invoke another trigger.

title: Send Email to Approvers when Dynamic Permissions are Used
description: Currently in self service actions, emails are not sent to the array of approvers which is generated via dynamic permissions. The behavior for dynamic permission's approvers needs to match that of static permission's approvers where emails are sent.

title: Action runs as blueprint
description:
The ability to have the blueprint capabilities on the audit log of action runs.

Currently, Port administrators must view the status of action runs (failure, success, awaiting approval, or in-progress) in the action runs audit log. Additionally, visualizations (pie chart and line chart) are limited to blueprints, and do not apply to action runs.

As an administrator, I would like to view the success rate of my action runs over time or in a pie chart.

title: Use current user's session to interact with internal systems
description:
We'd like to enable identity or user session propagation capabilities, allowing Self-Service Actions (SSAs) triggered within Port to be executed using the context and permissions of the currently logged-in user. When an authenticated user initiates an SSA that interacts with external systems or resources, the action should be performed on behalf of that user, inheriting their identity, role-based access controls (RBAC), and authorized privileges from the same Identity and Access Management (IAM) provider used by Port, which is Okta.

For example, if an employee triggers an SSA to update a ticket in a service management system like Jira, the update should be carried out using that employee's credentials and permissions within Jira, which are derived from the same Okta IAM provider that Port uses for authentication and authorization. Similarly, if an SSA involves provisioning resources in a cloud platform, it should leverage the logged-in user's identity and access rights from Okta to ensure the provisioning adheres to their authorized roles and scopes defined within the shared IAM provider.

By propagating the user's identity and session context from the common Okta IAM provider, we can maintain a consistent access control model across Port and integrated systems, ensuring that actions are performed with the appropriate level of authorization and adhering to the organization's security policies and governance rules defined within the centralized Okta IAM solution.

title: ScoreCard rule toggle button for catalog display
description: There are cases where the scorecard is governed by same property and different rule condition, this appears to be cluttered on the UI, requesting a toggle button or the feature in json for scorecard to enable/disable of having rule displayed on the catalog page for that particular entity.

title: Confirmation Window for Unsaved Changes in Self-service actions GUI Mode
description:
Add a confirmation window in the GUI mode in Self-service action window to prompt users when they attempt to navigate away from the page without saving their changes. Currently, this confirmation prompt exists in JSON mode in Self-service action window, but it is missing in GUI mode, which can lead to accidental data loss.

Rationale:

In the GUI mode, users may accidentally navigate away without saving their changes. A confirmation prompt will help prevent this, ensuring users have the chance to save their work before leaving the page. This feature is especially helpful for complex edits where re-entering data can be time-consuming.

Expected Behavior:

	•	Trigger: When a user tries to navigate away from the page while unsaved changes are present in GUI mode.

	•	Confirmation Prompt: The prompt should ask the user, “Are you sure you want to leave this page without saving changes?” with options to “Stay on Page” or “Leave without Saving.”

	•	Consistency: This behavior should be consistent with the existing confirmation prompt in JSON mode to ensure a seamless user experience across modes.

title: Enable dynamic user properties for actions conditions
description: Today using dynamic properties (getUserEmail, getUserTeams) is not available in day-2 action conditions, so that we will be able to have advanced filtering based on user relations

title: Support Calculated Properties in Self-Service Dataset Conditions
description: Currently, search conditions cannot be applied to calculated properties in self-service actions. Adding support for this is required

title: Allow form field default values to have complex patterns based on user selection
description:
In some cases, we may want to create a certain default value for a field based on previous selection made by the user. This can include literals and even multiple fields references.

The default value should be adjusted automatically until the field becomes visible.

title: RBAC for Folders
description:
We use folders to organize the catalog, and we have a dedicated folders for work-in-progress.

Today it is possible to configure permissions only at page level. We would like to be able to control permissions for entire folders as well so that e.g. any page added to the WIP folder will be visible only to Admins

title: Conditional Manual approval based on specific input
description: This FR is related to the ability to decide if a certain input in the action form is a certain value, enforce manual approval

title: Conditional step in Self-service form
description: For some actions, I would like to be able to display or not some steps. For example, I would like a step for selecting an entity if it exist, or display a step to create it if it is not exists already.

title: Support code or file upload in self-service action form
description:
Allow developers to upload or insert various configuration file types (e.g., .py, .conf, .txt) directly into the self service action form for "creating a microservice", for example. This feature should support a range of file formats beyond the current YAML, JSON, and Protobuf, and offer the option of markdown/free text input for added flexibility.

title: Configure timeout value for actions
description: Ability to configure timeout values for actions within Port so that certain operations, like deploying a service, do not exceed a certain duration.

title: AWS Cost Explorer API
description:
Can Port support ingesting AWS costs from the Cost explorer API?

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-cost-management/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html

There is an official aws plugin for backstage that does this

https://github.com/awslabs/backstage-plugins-for-aws/tree/main/plugins/cost-insights

The link provided here is no longer valid. 

https://roadmap.getport.io/ideas/p/aws-exporter-support-cloud-resources-costs

title: MCP Connector Tool Support in AI Agent Workflows
description: Enable AI agents to use tools from MCP connectors in automated workflows. A current workaround is to import data into the Port catalog, but this removes real-time access. Adding MCP connector support to agent workflows, with the same RBAC and audit controls, would allow more useful and flexible use cases.

title: Test connection when installing a new data source
description: Enable users to validate integration setup before full installation by testing connectivity, access, and basic permissions. Reduce setup errors and improve user confidence in integration correctness during onboarding.

title: Default on Form Load, Should be able to Clear when needed
description:
Currently default is being recalculated, whenever we clear it out.

The requirement is to have the default value populate only when the form is first loaded, rather than re-calculating it whenever it is removed.

title: Cancellation Logic For Self Service Actions
description: Add a cancel button to self service actions and allow configuration for the cancel button to invoke external communication.

title: Trigger worfklows upon related entity deletion and mirror property updates
Request to Increase Dynamic Approval Policy Query Threshold
description:
Currently, the dynamic approval policy returns a maximum of 1,000 entities per query. This creates a limitation for organizations with more than 1,000 users. In such cases, the policy cannot return the full set of eligible approvers, as some users fall beyond the 1,000-entity threshold and are therefore excluded from the results.

This request is to increase that threshold.

title: Manual Approvals | Show approvers
description:
When creating an action with approval you can't see who is the action approvers in the run page.

That can be helpful to know who can I reach to ask them to approve my run.

title: RBAC on Data sources
description: Today you can manage permissions on a Page, Self service, and blueprint level. Since some IDPs can have multiple "Builder" teams in different business domains, it would be ideal to have the option to define for each data source who has permissions to view the mapping, and modify it.

title: Actions Run widget | Ability to see all actions runs
description:
Today you have to choose one action when creating the action runs widget.

It can be powerful to create a table that shows the action runs of all actions (like in the global audit log)

title: Bulk self-service actions on entities
description: It would be great to have an option to do bulk actions(day2 and DELETE) on entities

title: File ingestion - JQ manipulation
description:
Currently, you can ingest files using the format

file_property: file://composer.lock

Being able to apply JQ at the file ingestion stage, will allow you to ingest less data to Port for a cleaner and faster portal, for example:

file_property: file://composer.lock | .myProperty

title: Show action permission changes in audit log
description:
Currently the audit log only shows when an action's permissions were updated, but it doesn't show what the actual permission changes are.

This is crucial for debugging permission issues and tracking changes.

title: Logs stream formatting
description:
It's nice to have some log stream formatting options. I like the approach Azure Devops uses.

Could you implement something like this:  

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/scripts/logging-commands?view=azure-devops&tabs=bash

Not sure if GitHub actions or Jenkins have something similar, to cover several CI/CD systems in a one shot, and highlight log lines automatically.

Additionally, to this, it's nice to have some console auto colouring support, like on the TF plan screenshot:

title: Dynamic user input validation
description:
Allow sending a validation requests with user inputs to the backend prior submitting the form.

For example, validate the user input for corectness against custom business logic, and display an error returned from the backend under the text field, without actually submitting the form. This way, the user has a chance to adjust the input, without having to re-submit the entire form with all the values again

title: OAuth2 / JWT backend for Self-service Actions
description:
As an admin, I would like to be able to setup a Self-Service Action which will call a REST API endpoint with the user token required by the API for authentication and authorization purpose (contrary to machine-to-machine token that can be implemented now).

For me as admin, I can set up the backend simply based on a few inputs: I tell to Port that i will call an OAuth2 endpoint, so I need to tell which authentication service I need to use. For that, previously, I set up the service in the admin (with credentials like the client_id, client_secret, ...).

On the user part, using this action will request an authentication workflow for the user to login to the targeted service (here github for the example) then Port will use the user token to call the Rest API endpoint.

The response (error or success) of the API can be logged in the Self Service Action report.

title: Port Teams Bot Backend
description:
We'd like to be able to Install a Port Teams Bot to our Microsoft 365 environment such that the bot can be authorised to communicate with members and channels in selected Teams Teams.

This could then be used as the backend in Self Service Actions to deliver messages to Teams or Users.

For example the recent Announcement feature could be connected to this proposed bot meaning the setup time to use that feature would be measured in minutes. Currently we've got to consider building our own backend service to handle the event from Port and figure out how to deliver into Teams. NOTE: Microsoft are end of life'ing the simpler WebHook method of posting to channels and pushing people towards building Bots and PowerActions... Not an ideal approach from a starting from zero context.

The vendor DX has produced their own Teams Bot to facilitate messaging users in Teams. As the customer configuring that capability it was very simple and straight forward. I think Port could build a bridge here too!

title: Multi line field
description:
Could you please amend the UI to include a pop-up dialog box that displays the entire string passed to the entity property on the catalog overview page?

The team is concerned about not being able to see the complete statement without copying and pasting it elsewhere to understand the full string.

Here's an example snippet where the issue occurs (highlighted: Justification): "This will allow us to access the VM from local desktop and VDI, Citrix etc for..."

Or make fields like description support longer strings.

title: Improve automation interface
description:
We will improve our interface for Automation (to match with one of Actions) to simplify the creation of new automation.

Some early preview screenshots are attached!

title: Configurable Minimum Approval Threshold for Manual Approvals (e.g., “2 out of N”)
description: Support configuring a minimum number of required approvers for actions that require manual approval (e.g., “at least 2 approvers” or “2 out of N”), as the current options only allow either a single approver (“Any”) or requiring all approvers (“All”). While dynamic permissions can define who is eligible to approve, they do not control how many approvals are required. Introducing a configurable approval threshold (such as a fixed number or majority) would provide greater flexibility and eliminate the need for workarounds.

title: Support live events in AWS V3
Support additional granular role permissions
description: Add support for creating and managing additional roles to improve flexibility in permissions.

title: Dynamically set the self-service action approval step
description:
Add the ability to dynamically decide whether the self-service action will have an approval step or not.

How it will work - upon the action execution, a webhook can be sent to the customer's backend in order to run a logic that will decide if this specific action run needs to be approved by someone before executed

title: Ordering of action widgets
description: The ability to order how the self serve action widgets appear on the hub page. At the moment it seems they can just be in the order in which they were created?

title: Per‑User Impersonation / Delegated Execution for Actions
description:
We need Port to support executing self‑service actions as the real user, not as a shared technical account. Today, actions that call tools like GitHub or Jira are executed with an app token, so in those tools every change appears as coming from a generic user. This breaks per‑user traceability required by an external zero‑trust banking audit, is considered a high security risk, and blocks us from safely scaling self‑service to 1,500+ engineers and multiple companies in our group.

Requested capability:

* OAuth2‑based delegated authorization so each Port user can link their own GitHub/Jira account and actions run with their token.

* A consistent “execute as user” model across integrations (GitHub first, then Jira, others later).

* Configurable backend for actions: keep current “machine token” mode, and add a new user‑session/OAuth mode that respects Port RBAC and IdP policies.

This is a blocker for audit compliance, enterprise‑wide adoption, and for comparing Port fairly with other IDPs that already support per‑user execution.

title: Expose Catalogue Usage Telemetry
description:
As a Platform Engineer launching a new dashboard in the Port catalogue I'd like to 1) track adoption and usage of the new dashboard/page and 2) have access to data so I can integrate my surveying tooling to survey the users who use the new dashboard.

For big picture context. We are also a customer of DX who have a product called PlatformX. We have integrated this into our Self Service Actions. When a user (Bob) runs a self-service action via Port an event is fired off to DX saying that Bob did X event. DX looks to see if Bob is eligible for surveying based on the action (event) taken and if valid will send a survey to them personally on teams (MS Bot framework). This gives a very low friction option for Bob to provide feedback they might have otherwise not raised.

We'd like to perform a similar integration but for important pages in the catalogue, like a newly launched dashboard. So, the user experience might be that Bob accesses the new port dashboard page for the first time and sometime later is pinged on teams saying "Hey we saw you used the ABC dashboard for the first time. Could you let us know what you thought etc..."

Currently we don't have access to data that tells us who has accessed what pages in the catalogue at what time. Could this data/event telemetry be made available?

title: Catalog auto-discovery
description:
Currently, relating blueprints and their entities to one another can be done with ease using jq in the data source mapping. While this is helpful, it would be beneficial if Port could auto-discover and propose relations between certain things.

The new "Catalog Discovery" feature will provide the ability to automatically discover new catalog entities and their relations.

For example, Port will discover all your Services and their relations to the different third-party tools, such as Git Repository, PagerDuty, Snyk, Sonar, etc.

title: Create pages using AI
description:
Allows users to generate pages using AI in Port. The vibe-coded page leverages Port’s rich context lake and answers a business question or analysis need, for example a manager asking for a quick snapshot of ownership, risk, progress, or gaps across teams.

See a few ideas for mock-ups.

title: Support custom kind (API endpoint) in out of the box integrations
description:
Today, out of the box Ocean integrations come with a fixed set of predefined kinds. 

When users want to ingest data from API endpoints that are not covered by those kinds, they either need to wait for Port to add a new kind or create a separate custom Ocean integration, including authentication and connection setup, even though they already have an existing integration configured. 

This creates unnecessary friction and duplication. We should allow users to define custom kinds directly within out of the box Ocean integrations, reusing the existing authentication and connection that Port already manages, so they can fetch additional data from supported APIs without creating a new integration or waiting for Port to add more kinds

title: Conditional widget display
description:
I would like to conditionally show or hide widgets in my entity dashboard based on some property on my blueprint. 

For example, have a Service blueprint with a type of "Frontend" would display Frontend specific widgets or dashboard tabs

title: Add Codefresh as a supported Backend for an Action triggered from Port
description:
Basically, add Codefresh here:

https://docs.getport.io/create-self-service-experiences/setup-backend/

More specifically, the Action in Port should be able to trigger a [Classic Codefresh Pipeline](https://codefresh.io/docs/docs/pipelines/introduction-to-codefresh-pipelines/) ([link](https://codefresh.io/docs/docs/pipelines/introduction-to-codefresh-pipelines/)), not to be confused with an Argo Workflows|Events pipeline.

title: Apply one scorecard to multiple blueprints
description:
As a builder, having one scorecard applying to one blueprint means I need to create 3 scorecards for the same criteria which causes friction in the creation, maintenance and visualization of these. 

Longer description:

- The same requirement exists across different resource types like deployable units, repos, and host-based apps.

- With Port’s current model, we need a separate scorecard per blueprint, which turns one concept into many parallel scorecards.

- That creates a maintenance problem as they could quickly grow into dozens of scorecards and make the team the bottleneck for setup and upkeep.

- We also want to support unified views of the resulting action items and health status, instead of splitting them across blueprint-specific scorecards.

title: Prisma Cloud Ocean integration
description: Ingest vulnerabilities from Prisma Cloud for open source, containers and other sources

title: Ability to specify the source of an API change (updatedByAlias/createdByAlias)
description:
We now have multiple locations where we are using the API to update specific blueprints. Having all changes to blueprints made through the API under "Rest API" is too vague for us to know where specifically the change came from. It would be nice if we could include a name of the source in our blueprint change payload and then be able to see this reflect in the audit logs.

For example:

I change blueprint Service with a python script called "service_changer.py" using a POST in the script - I can also pass into the body of the POST "updatedByAlias":"service_changer.py"

And then later, I can filter the audit log by "updatedByAlias":"service_changer.py" to see all changes made through that specific script.

title: Support jq version 1.8 in Port
description: Port currently uses JQ v1.7.1, which does not support functions introduced in v1.8 (e.g., trim, ltrim, rtrim). This causes confusion when users follow the latest jq documentation or test queries in the official playground. Upgrading to v1.8 would enable these functions, remove the need for regex workarounds, and align Port’s capabilities with the latest jq features across self-service actions, mappings, and exporters.

title: API to return action approver details
description: Currently, the API only displays the user ID, status, and description of an action. It would be beneficial if it could also include the action approver details, such as their name and email.

title: Widget to display automation runs
description: Currently, the ability to create widgets is only available for actions. We would like to have a widget to view the runs of automations also.

title: Show login attempts in the audit log
description: Make it possible to see login attempts (both successful and unsuccessful) in an organization's audit log

title: "Preview" self-service action input type
description:
The "preview" self-service action input will provide a way to display the user's static data that helps while filling out the action form.

This is done by calculating values based on the data of other form inputs, user data, and entity data.

For example - creating a "Preview" input for a "full name" that will display the full name according to the "first name" and "last name" inputs

title: Filters UI as an input inside a self‑service action form
description: A feature that allows end‑users to use the Filters UI as an input inside a self‑service action form, and on submission, pass the resulting filter JSON so it can be used (e.g., with the Search API) to fetch matching services.

title: Admins should see the HTTP response of action backend's webhook calls
description: As an admin, I'd like to see the return status and body for webhook self-service action backends

title: Additional GitHub Metrics
description: We would like to have additional GitHub Metrics come natively from the GItHub integration, for example the ones from this repo https://github.com/port-experimental/super-github-metrics

title: DORA Metrics for Azure Devops
description:
Support of DORA Metrics for ADO as part of Experience 360

Out of the box ADO metrics support

title: Embed docs in installation modal
description:
Embed the documentation directly in the integration-installation modal.

This keeps users in flow, gives them step-by-step guidance without switching tabs, and helps prevent setup or permissions slip-ups.

title: Identify the first commit & timestamp associated with a "Deployment"
description: Add support for reliably identifying the earliest commit & timestamp that belongs to a "Deployment" across GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps, as this is required to calculate Lead Time for Changes regarding DORA metrics.

title: Allow agregating owning teams from multiple parent blueprints
description: Have a blueprint to inherit owning teams from multiple blueprints and agregate the teams. I.e. In a model with Application > Project > Portfolio blueprints, Application should be able to inherit ownership from both Project and Portfolio, while Project should be able to inherit from Portfolio while also having its own owning teams (i.e. project may have a 'Managers' team that can manage that project and Applications on it but not the entire Porftolio).

title: Team inheritance support OR relationships
description:
At present it supports inheritance from a single blueprint.

Where you have multiple blueprints which a PR entity can be associated with  e.g.

- Microservice

- Tooling

- Library

Would be nice to add OR tooling OR library where a relation doesn't exist on the initial check to complete the coverage of options for inheritance

title: Audit Log for Pages
description: Provide audit log functionality for pages so that we can track which users create/edit/delete things like dashboards.

title: Self service action without requiring blueprint
description:
As a DevOps Engineer,

I want the ability to create self-service actions directly within Port without the need for predefined blueprints,

So that I can quickly and flexibly introduce new processes and tasks tailored to my specific needs.

title: Webhook resiliency
description:
Currently, the webhook integration does not allow you to reingest failed events, or recover from incidents with the integration.

Implementing a Dead Letter Queue or an alternative mechanism that lets you redeliver events received by the webhook integration will improve the integration resiliency.

title: Support manual approval in the middle of a running action
description:
Today manual approval can only be configured as a gate to prevent an action from starting.

In some real-life workflows, an action might perform some process and then arrive at another point that requires manual approval.

Port should support such cases by making it possible to update the state of a running action, allowing it to require approval again (maybe even from different approvers) and only then continue its work, probably by sending an approve request to the pipeline system that is currently stuck

title: Place action in maintenance mode
description:
Sometimes when an action is going through changes, a platform engineer would want to disable an action for maintenance purposes.

It would be great to be able to temporarily disable actions for non-admins.

title: "Cancel" button for action run
description: Ability to cancel the execution of an action after triggering it

title: Re-run capability for Workflow runs
description:
Requesting re-run button/capability for workflow runs.

During development and testing, we have to create a new event every time we want to test a workflow change. Being able to re-run a previous workflow run would significantly speed up the iteration cycle.

title: Email type invocation method for automations
description:
The ability to choose the invocation method of an automation to be "Sending an email"

For example - Whenever a scorecard is degraded, send an update email (Just like the Slack use case, but sending the report in email)

title: Update audit log for Users & Team entities to show what user made the change
description: Currently I can see that a change to a User or Team was made, I cannot see who made it. The audit log record only shows "updated by": "port-internal" as in the screenshot as opposed to an actual user. This is important for compliance auditing

title: Abilty to add a filter so only certain Self Service Actions appear on a Catalog Page.
description: When using overarching blueprints such as "components", which have many types including micro-frontends, microservices, connectors, It is important to differentiate these by using different catalogue pages. This can be achieved, however we then have a need to only show specific self service actions on those pages. For instance, there is no requirement to surface the SSA for creation of a microservice on our micro-frontend catalogue page. Therefore there is a requirement to filter Self Service Actions on custom catalogue pages.

title: Table & bulk actions
description:
There are two situations I find myself in on any table view with day-2 actions:

1. I want to bulk run all actions (I know that there is a feature request for this)

2. I want to run a single action that references all entities

This second case is something I would call "table actions", or it could just be another standard create action.

Some example cases:

- I apply some filters, and I now want to associate all the filtered entities with another entity (e.g. assign team)

- I apply filters and I want to reference all the existing entities as part of a payload to creating an incident, sending a slack, etc...

title: SSO Group integration - easily control the list of allowed groups
description:
Currently, the only way to determine what groups will be synced with Port is by creating REGEX and sending it to the Port team to implement.

We would like to have the ability to easily control the groups' allow list via Port's UI/API

title: I want to be able to use multiple backends for one self service action
description:
As an example: I have different GH actions configured for provisioning resources on AWS depending on the resource requested:

- Action A: To provision an EC2 instance

- Action B: To provision an S3 bucket

- Action C: To provision an AWS user

- Action D: To provision a lambda function

- Action E: To provision a Postgres DB

I have a single SSA, "Provision AWS Resource" which contains several advanced inputs which are visible or disappear based on the resource type selected. Due to Port's current setup, I have to combine these 5 GH actions into one since the SSA can only trigger one backend. This will cause my GH action to be huge, convoluted and complex, when I could just configure my SSA to send a payload to a backend (GH action A - E) depending on the resource to be provisioned.

Also, I should be able to configure the format of the payload per backend. This allows a single generic SSA but different branches of GH actions (or a different backend pipeline) to be used for complex use cases.

title: Support Board view in Table widget (aka Kanban)
description: Support a Kanban board, allowing to drag items, etc.

title: Teams, roles and dynamic policy in Port Workflows Input node
description: Right now the Input node supports only a static list of users. Adding teams, roles, and dynamic policies will enable more advanced human-in-the-loop use cases. For example: requesting approval from the on-call engineer before deployment outside business hours.

title: Apply new/updated Automation to all existing entities
description:
Most of the time, when we create an automation, we'd like to apply it to all existing entities so they will all get aligned based on the automation and then the automation will be triggered for new events.

Currently, the entities will get aligned only after all of them will get the respective event which potentially can take a lot of time. 

Having something similar to Gmail filters' "Also apply filter to X matching conversations" feature would really improve the UX of automation as today we need to manually resync or do a dummy migration in order to trigger the automation alignment.

title: In-app notifications of changes to entities
description: Right now, Port admins can create automations that can, for example, upsert entities to create a "changelog" type of experience. While this can be an acceptable method for "notifying" entity owners about changes to their entities, a better solution would be in-app notifications in Port to notify the owning team whenever a project or an environment changes

title: Upsert entity invocation method - Allow upserting multiple entities
description: Today you can only update one entity using the Upsert entity invocation method, It's true that as a workaround you can send an api call to a custom webhook and update multiple entities using the custom webhook, but it'll be ideal and much clearer to have this ability in the invocation method itself

title: Action Runs API endpoint improvements
description:
The /v1/actions/runs is currently limited because there is not enough ability for filtering of the returned runs, there is no "include" parameter, and the limit is set to max of 1000 runs without ability for pagination. 

The endpoint can be improved by adding support for

- Filtering by run status (and other fields)

- "include" parameter

- Pagination

title: "My Teams" Filter Should Restrict Users With No Team Membership
description: When a dashboard or catalog uses the “My Teams” filter, users who are not part of any team currently see all entities because the filter resolves to an empty set and removes restrictions; instead, the filter should return zero results (or follow a defined fallback) for users with no team membership, ensuring they don’t see everything by default, regardless of their role.

title: Action runs - update log messages.
description:
Currently, there is no way to edit current action logs.

A possible solution will be to return a message ID when posting a log through the API, and implementing a new route to patch messages based on the ID.

This will help keep the logs cleaner and save a lot of space.

title: Audit log for user management
description:
Capture user management activities (names and time stamps) in the audit log. For example:

- when user was invited / created / deleted

- who invited / edited / deleted user

- when user permissions changed

- who changed user permissions

- how the user was created (API, UI, etc)

title: Client Secret Rotation Alert
description: We want to configure an alert that is sent out to admins when an organization secret has been changed.  Or perhaps, a way to subscribe to a Port event that says “this client’s secret was rotated.”

title: Self-service action dynamic display
description:
Currently, the current RBAC model (https://docs.getport.io/actions-and-automations/create-self-service-experiences/set-self-service-actions-rbac/dynamic-permissions/) only allows administrators to filter self-service action visibility based on teams or role.

This feature request is about the possibility to use a more complex approach based on properties from user profile or from the team properties of which he is a part of. 

Kind of the field "policy" but which can't be used for this purpose today.

title: Restrictions on Running Actions in Parallel
description:
As an admin of Port,

I want to be able to configure restrictions on running actions in parallel, so that I can control the concurrency of certain tasks within my workflow. For example, I don't want to run a deployment action on the same service twice.

title: Add Table input to Self Service Action Form
description:
It would be great if Port Self Service Actions allowed to have an input field in table format for users. We need users to input multiple times 4 related inputs which would be better visualized as a table (this is how we manage it in another tool currently). Without a table view, the UX is not good. Use case:

- Developers need to input network information

- This information is in a table naturally (DNS | IP | Port | Something else)

- The information may need to be inputted multiple times in a form

- They need to make sure the data matches the other data (DNS with IP and such)

title: JQ in Action conditions
description:
Right now it is not possible to use JQ when creating conditions for Day-2 or Delete actions. 

It would be very powerful to have that possibility for advanced searching/filtering of entities

title: Retry logic for transient errors in action backends
description:
It would be nice to have the option to have Port manage back pressure and retries of action runs.

It would require action run implementations to be idempotent and some way to opt in for Port-managed retries through the API. 

Maybe a status field on the action run signalling a transient error and that Port should retry after applying backoff.

title: Add Webhook Secret Support for Ocean Metrics
description: Currently, Ocean metrics webhooks only support passing a webhook URL, adding support for webhook secrets to enhance the security of metrics data sent from Ocean integrations to monitoring endpoints

title: Modify Payload/Inputs for 'Waiting for approval' Self-Service Actions
description:
Currently, once a user initiates a self-service action that needs approval, the action's payload or inputs are fixed. Approvers are unable to change the action's specifics and they can only accept or reject it. 

I suggest before giving final approval, approvers will be able to make any necessary changes to the payload or inputs, potentially reducing the number of rounds of back-and-forth correspondence required between initiators and approvers to modify payloads and inputs.

title: receive the relation objects in the payload instead of just the related object identifier
description:
Right now when you query an entity using API you will get the identifiers of the related entities. 

It could be helpful to receive the relation objects in the payload instead of just the related object identifier

title: Toggle Payload 'See Details' for Self-Service Actions
description: In the action run, the payload 'See details' is available by default to all users. Need a toggle to turn it on/off for the self-service actions.

title: Manual approval | support approval notification to a Kafka topic
Port GitHub action | Support dry run for the Port action for tests
description: Sometimes we want to run Github workflows for tests purposes to see no error is raised. So we would want to have a flag for the port-github-action (https://github.com/marketplace/actions/port-github-action) to dry run it only for validation

title: Improved Retry Mechanism for Port Synchronization
description:
The current retry mechanism in Port does not handle well synchronization failures caused by race conditions and temporary issues. This feature request proposes an enhanced retry system to improve data consistency and reliability with eventual consistency.

1. Automated Re-sync for Specific Blueprints (based on missing realations)

Add support for automated re-sync based on missing relations in blueprint entities.

- Improve the current periodic re-sync feature to support specific blueprints

- Add support for configuring conditional re-sync only if there are errors caused by missing relations

This will ensure eventual consistency for objects with infrequent updates (e.g., re-sync only for k8s namespaces when k8s pod has missing namespace as a relation)

2. Implement Exponential Backoff

- Replace the current retry system with an exponential backoff mechanism

- Gradually increase the time between retry attempts to reduce system load and improve success rates

3. Retry for Relation Sync Issues

- Enable retry attempts specifically for entities created with relation sync issues

- Target scenarios where related entities may not have been imported yet due to timing

Benefits

- More efficient use of system resources during retries

- Higher success rate for entity synchronization

- Automatic resolution of temporary inconsistencies

- Improved data integrity and completeness over time

This feature will enhance Port's ability to maintain consistent and complete data, especially in complex scenarios involving multiple related entities and large-scale imports.

title: Trigger Aggregation Property Update
description:
Some aggregation properties will only be updated when certain conditions are met e.g. total number of related x to y could only update for any entity change in a related x. Some aggregation properties are also usually static after an initial period of updating and will likely never be updated again. 

For these recalculating every 15 minutes will result in lots of unnecessary work. What if instead these aggregation properties could be triggered by an update to a downstream related entity either before or after so only have an update when necessary. So when an entity of x is updated the aggregation update is triggered for the before y and after y. 

The reduction in work and processing could even mean this type of aggregation could avoid the limit for aggregation properties.

An automation could even be used to trigger the relevant updates as this can already handle the any change to the relation logic and would impose rate limits making sure the amount of updates stays sensible

title: ADO SaaS Integration : support for multiple organizations
AI Plugin Registry
description:
Goal: Discover, view, and govern all agents, skills, prompts, commands across the organization with hierarchical scopes and approval workflows so that you can standardize AI tooling and prevent agentic sprawl.

Business Outcome: Single source of truth for AI entities; eliminate duplicates and shadow; enforce quality standards before distribution.

title: Entities table performance improvements
description:
Currently, the entities table's performance degrades significantly when loading a large number of entities.

As part of this item, we would like to incorporate improvements that will:

- Shorten the load time

- Prevent browser crashes and cases where a large table degrades the overall page/dashboard performance

title: Kind ownership
description:
Currently, the GitHub integration can't be set up with multiple instances, which means that only one instance is owning all entities. 

This becomes problematic when you want to have two kinds populate the same entities. The reason for that, is the query field can result in an entity being deleted from the "enriching kind" rather than the "owning kind".

Suggestion: Add to entities created by the GitHub app a new type of ownership, based on the mapping kind. This will allow only specific kinds to delete entities from the catalog, while allowing other kinds to safely "enrich" the entities.

title: ServiceNOW DORA metrics
description: Implement integration level metrics for MTTR and Change Failure Rate.

title: Add real-time pre-execution status and progress visibility for self-service actions
description:
Users see no feedback while jobs are waiting to start (e.g. due to GitHub API rate limits causing 8–15+ min delays). There is no indication of whether the action is queued, rate-limited, or encountered an error during startup.

Requested behavior:

> Surface early startup/progress states (e.g. "queued," "delayed," "rate-limited") before the workflow produces logs

> Show meaningful errors if the job fails to start

> Apply across all self-service action types

title: Add "Select All" / "Deselect All" for Array-Type Entity Inputs in Self-Service Action Forms
description: Currently, there is no "Select All" or "Deselect All" option available for array-type entity inputs in self-service action forms, requiring users to manually select each item one by one — which becomes tedious and time-consuming when dealing with large lists. We'd like to request the addition of a "Select All" / "Deselect All" toggle or checkbox at the top of array-type entity input dropdowns, so users can bulk select or deselect all available items with a single click, significantly reducing friction and improving usability for anyone working with large arrays in self-service action forms.

title: It would be powerful to be able to run javascript or python code to extract form field values from external sources via API calls
description: Lack of ability to run scripts on Port JS/PS/python

title: Conditional Team Inheritance based on $team Value
description: Currently, if team inheritance is enabled, setting $team through the UI or API is not allowed. It would be nice to enable 'Team inheritance' only if the $team value is not set explicitly during mapping.

title: Make “Owning teams” (ownership) configurable as a required field on blueprints
description:
Current behavior: Ownership is defined via the ownership property on a blueprint. It is optional, and even when configured as Direct or Inherited, the “Owning teams” field is not enforceable as required at entity creation time.

Requested change: Add the ability to configure the “Owning teams” (ownership) field as required per blueprint, so that when creating or registering an entity of that blueprint, the operation can be rejected if no owning team is set.

Why this is needed: To enforce clear ownership and accountability for every Service.

title: Actions audit log improvements
description:
In addition to the general action runs audit log, a specific audit log for each action will be added to the "audit log" page

Each action log will display as columns the general details of each run (ID, status, start, end) and also the specific inputs of the action inputted by the user who executed it.

title: Actions - Port Hosted Option & Lambda Invocation
description:
It would be awesome to see Port hosted actions at some point in the future. Whether you utilize an existing standard, such as GitHub Action's workflow syntax, or come up with your own, being able to not have to link out externally from port for smaller actions, or creating cron-type actions from Port would be awesome. Additionally, it would allow for Port to include their own marketplace for actions without relying on 3rd party integrations that may or may not exist for each tenant.

To this, another invocation type that would be awesome, would be directly integrating with Lambda and OpenFAAS. I know this is possible by using WebHooks to get there eventually, but skipping the additional step to be able to just run the Lambda would be awesome.

To tie these two together - If you integrate with OpenFAAS, you basically get an awesome integration for port-hosted openfaas or self-hosted.

title: Self-service action user input types
description:
Is it possible to differentiate between the existing "Text" (which translates to a simple input field) and a more expansive "Text area" (which would translate to a text area input field)?

We have a few use cases where we were trying to avoid the overhead of formatted text/adding an extra click to interact with the markdown editor, and really just focused on a bit more visual space for both the input and display of plain, unformatted text. Consider the example of the description for a portal feedback item in the demo site - something like [this](https://demo.getport.io/portal_use_case_requestEntity?identifier=more-markdowns), where I was imagining that the description might render on multiple lines and/or two columns, instead of needing to hover to see the full text.

title: Dynamic titles/labels in self-service action forms
description: Allow self-service action input titles/labels (and standalone title/description blocks in forms) to be set dynamically based on .entity / .form data. This would let action builders display context-aware text (like including selected entity properties or previous input values) directly in the form labels and explanatory text, improving clarity for end users.

title: Title and description within action forms
description: For long forms, I sometimes want to add a bit more context for upcoming inputs or add some visual separation between inputs on the same step. It would be great to be able to insert some text on its own in a form.

title: Support multi-line input for secrets input type
description: Currently multi-line is only available for text inputs, but we would like it to be supported for secret inputs as well.

title: MCP should enforce frontend-only input validations when executing SSAs
description:
Request to implement consistent guardrail enforcement when triggering self-service actions via the MCP, so that dataset filters and advanced input logic are respected regardless of the execution surface (UI or API/MCP).

Currently, the Port MCP bypasses frontend-only input validations (like dataset filters) when self service actions are triggered, allowing LLMs to select any value, which can violate intended permissions/guardrails.

title: Regex Validation for Title Key
description:
It would be very useful to support regex validation on the title key, similar to how regex validation can already be applied to string properties.

Reference: 

https://docs.port.io/build-your-software-catalog/customize-integrations/configure-data-model/setup-blueprint/properties/string/#validate-string

title: Add conditionals based on bool input
description:
I want to be able based on bool input to populate other property or hide it/grey out. For example if input1 true create array to select from in input2 else hide input2

This way we can add logic based on input boolean and use one action to perform complex workflows

title: Running JQ manipulation on dynamic filters
description: Currently you can't  run JQ manipulation on dynamic filters. If we could, we could connect to entities using jq filtering (like getting name from email)

title: Enable Selection of Specific Events for Webhook Testing
description: Currently, when a webhook integration is created and events are passed to Port, there's no option to choose the event type when clicking "load latest event." We need the ability to select specific events, especially when a single webhook handles multiple event types (e.g., 2 to 3 different events).

title: Configure action permissions using Port's pulumi provider
description: At the moment we are not able to configure an action's permissions using the pulumi provider. An update needs to be made to support this

title: Retry logic for automation runs
description: It would be helpful to have the option for Automations to automatically handle errors and retry runs whenever the initial execution fails due to backend issues. This would improve reliability and reduce the need for manual intervention in transient failure scenarios.

title: Terraform Provider | Users roles resource
Historical Reporting for Deleted Entities
description:
Port currently only displays entities that exist in the catalog. Users need the ability to generate historical reports that include deleted entities, particularly for:

Tracking entity counts over time (including deleted entities)

Visualizing entity duration/lifetime after deletion

Analyzing trends for entities with timer properties that expire automatically

Current Gap: Line charts and dashboards only reflect current entities; deleted entities are only available in the audit log (limited to 1,000 records) with no visualization capabilities.

Requested Solution: Enable historical reporting and visualization features that persist data beyond entity deletion, allowing comprehensive analytics across the full lifecycle of entities.

title: Have back button in catalog entity view take you back to the catalog
description:
When using the catalog page to view an entity, the back button takes you back to the last page in your browser window history, and not back to the entity catalog.

This means that if you open an entity in a new tab it won't do anything, and if you paste the entity link in an existing tab it would take you back to the previous page you were on (that might be unrelated to Port).

It would be nice if the back button would take you back to the catalog.

Attaching a video demonstrating the current behavior.

title: GitHub integration - Use GitHubs search for campaigns on Gradle, HCL files, and more
description: The ability to grep on git repo files via regex, so we can do campaigns on Java, sb3.x, terraform as they are files present in the repo. Today it's possible mostly using bringing the whole file and having a calculation property / using a script of your own.

title: Improve Webhook Data Source Card Blueprint Display
description:
Currently, webhook data source cards display all blueprints that have ever been successfully ingested through them. Even after the mappings for certain blueprints are removed, those blueprints continue to appear in the data source card. This can cause confusion and unnecessary clutter, as the card no longer reflects the active mappings.

It would be much more helpful if the card displayed only the currently mapped blueprints, ensuring that the information remains up to date, and relevant.

title: Expose Approver Context in Runs
description: Currently, SSA execution context only includes the run creator, not the actual approver. There’s no way to display the approver’s name or email in entity today. This would be a nice improvement to add

title: Show logs when hovering on an action in the side menu
description:
Right now when you trigger a self-service action, a menu appears on the right hand side of Port. By hovering over the running action icon, you can see some information about the action such as the title, related entity and trigger time.

It would be very convenient to also include a tail of the latest logs of the action as it is running in that hover. The hover view is rather small so it would probably be best to limit it to 10 log lines to avoid clutter.

title: Allow use of external Claude managed agents
description: Ability to add CDN embed code to reference external AI Agent that I built using a tool such as n8n. See: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@n8n/chat.

title: "Finally" or "catch-all" failure branch in Workflows
description:
Request for a top-level `onWorkflowFailure` handler, or a reserved `finally` branch on workflow definitions.

Today, there's no way to reliably trigger a notification (Slack, PagerDuty, etc.) when a workflow fails without compromising the workflow's final status. The current options available are:

onFailure: terminate — correctly marks the workflow FAILED, but downstream notification nodes never run.

onFailure: continue — notification nodes run, but the overall workflow is marked SUCCESS despite the upstream failure.

Impact: Can't easily implement basic alerting without misrepresenting operational health.

title: Tenable Cloud Integration
description: Per title, integrate with Tenable Cloud

title: HashiCorp Vault for Secrets Management in Port Actions/Workflows
description:
When triggering webhooks or direct orchestrator calls from Port Self-Service Actions or Workflows, Port currently requires secrets (API keys, tokens) to be stored within Port itself. For organizations with strict infosec policies — where all secrets must reside exclusively in HashiCorp Vault — this is a blocker.

The workaround today is to route through a CI system (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.) that handles the Vault key exchange, but this introduces an unwanted dependency for teams using a direct orchestrator pattern where the orchestrator feeds execution feedback back into Port.

Requested Capability:

Native support for HashiCorp Vault as a secrets backend for Port Actions/Workflows — allowing Port to resolve secrets at runtime from Vault rather than storing them locally.

Use Case:

Customer: Sophos (via Nuno Pinto)

Trigger: Self-Service Action → direct webhook/orchestrator call requiring authenticated API keys

Constraint: Infosec policy mandates all secrets stored in HashiCorp Vault only

Current gap: No native Vault secrets resolution; CI workaround not viable for their direct-trigger architecture

title: Self-Service Actions to automatically tie affected entities to an action run
description:
Currently it's only possible tying entities to an action run by manually sending an API request to  the entities with the `run_id` - https://docs.port.io/actions-and-automations/reflect-action-progress/#tying-entities-to-an-action-run

I'm thinking this should be automated when invoking a self service actions - User clicks on an action --> port system gets the entities affected and encodes them with an action runner run_id - instead of the back and forth in our backend of retrieving both the entities and the action run ourselves and patching them.

title: True Change Detection for Self-service Actions like Data Sources has
description:
When you open the edit dialog for a self-service action and close it, it will ask you if you want to continue editing or discard changes whether you made changes or not, this can be confusing because if you had it open for a little while and are actively building it out, you might forget whether you did make changes or not, of course you can simply always save, but it would be nice if a true diff check was made to see if a change is actually present and if not it would simply exit the dialog without asking for confirming about changes that do not exist.

Data Sources dialogs already do this, when you edit them you can close without being prompted for confirmation if you made no changes.

title: Approver ↔ Requester communication thread on action runs
description: When a self-service action is in `WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL` status, both the approver and the requester should be able to exchange messages/comments directly within the action run context in Port. This would eliminate the need for out-of-band communication (e.g., Slack DMs) and keep all context in one place. It would also reduce the friction of having to decline → resubmit cycles just to clarify inputs.

title: Deny action in permissions configuration
description:
At now If Administrator wants to add possibility to edit only one field then user/role has to be removed from entities.update roles/users path and this user/role has to be added to particular property under updateProperties path.

If Administrator wants to prohibit edit only one properties from set of 10 or more properties then configuration is a little complex.

The deny action can help and then Administrator can add deny action only to property that user should not be able to edit - e.g $identifier

title: RBAC for Port Usage Dashboard
description:
Current behavior

The Usage Dashboard is automatically visible to all Org Admins in Pro & Enterprise orgs. [Usage dashboard announcement]

This access cannot be changed or restricted today; all Org Admins always see it.

Problem

Usage and billing‑related data is sensitive. Organizations want least‑privilege access and the ability to limit visibility to a small group (e.g., platform owners, FinOps, auditors), not all Org Admins. 

Requested change

Add RBAC controls for the Usage Dashboard

Configure who can view it by:

Roles

Specific users

Teams

This should be similar in spirit to existing page permissions (view/edit by roles/users/teams). 

Configurable default behavior

Keep current default (all Org Admins) for backward compatibility, but allow organizations to override it (e.g., restrict to selected roles/users/teams)

Impact

Better alignment with least‑privilege and compliance requirements.

Consistent RBAC story across Port (catalog pages, dashboards, and platform‑level features like Usage Dashboard).

title: Allow catalog page to have custom policy for viewing the page
description:
At this time, catalog pages only allow for static users and teams to have access (view) to the catalog page.

We want to be able to do something similar to self-service actions where we can set up a custom policy that looks at properties of a user.

A use case we are looking for is that we wanted some catalog pages to only be accessible to managers.

Managers are identified by a flag on the user blueprint.

title: MyTeams filter should appear in all filter dropdowns
description:
The MyTeams option should appear in the filter value dropdown whenever the selected filter property resolves to a team, regardless of whether that property is:

- A native owning team property on the directly filtered entity

- A computed team property on the directly filtered entity

- An owning team property or relation on a related entity (i.e. filtering Entity A by Entity B's owning team)

This can currently be achieved using JSON mode filters, but not in the form view with MyTeams.

title: Audit log streaming to a data warehouse
description: Support streaming audit logs to a customer-managed data warehouse bucket, enabling customers to monitor Port activity in near real time.

title: Dynamic Self Service Action
description: It would be great to have the ability to dynamically create multiple entities through a self-service action using a "+" button. For example, creating multiple CosmosDB containers. Currently, we have two self-service actions: one that creates a single CosmosDB container, and another that provisions multiple containers using a JSON list. However, the latter bypasses the regex validations that are applied in the single-container provisioning action.

title: Triggering a self-service action from somewhere other than the self-service page
description:
Now that a deep link to a specific self-service action is available, we have taken advantage to link directly to a self-service action. Specifically, we have made a similar portal feedback mechanism to the one offered in the demo site, and then added a hyperlink within the description of a given page like "Have feedback about this page?" which is hyperlinked to the "Leave feedback about the portal" Day 2 action. 

Unfortunately, this link takes the user to the Self-service page (albeit with the correct action modal opened to the form). Completing the form then leaves then on the Self-service page. Similar to how related self service actions are handled within an entity table or from an action card, it would be nice to have a way to trigger the display of the appropriate self-service action form as a modal over the page that the user is currently (perhaps with some opinionated/specially handled markdown syntax to designate creating a link to trigger the display of a specific self-service action?).

title: Auto-generate action inputs from blueprint definition
description:
Right now if you want to create an action that includes as inputs the exact same properties that exist on a blueprint, that action has to be created and its inputs need to be configured manually.

But since it is quite common that action inputs closely resemble the blueprints they are defined on, it would save a lot of time and configuration to just create a new blueprint action with an “input copy” of the blueprint properties. The user will then have the option to customize the action inputs as he needs, but a lot of the initial work of replicating the blueprint properties as inputs again will be saved.

title: Support entity dropdown for all relation filter operators
description: When filtering a catalog table by a relation, the entity selection dropdown is currently only available for the `has any of` operator. Since multiple operators are supported when filtering by a relation, the dropdown should be available across all of them for consistency.

title: Dynamic Default in Actions
description:
Allow an input with the default keyword which is dependent on another one of the inputs to updated dynamically when the related input is.

E.g. if the first input is an entity selector and the second is name which has a default of `.entity.title` allow the name to be updated as the entity is

This is currently possible with the dataset keyword which will update when the related entity is updated so would like similar with the default keyword

title: Hide Client secret value in UI
description: When I go to "credentials" tab I see secrets values, it may be a critical point when I work  this and share my screen. I would be nice to hide the Client secret value by default (both Organization and Personal), make it blurred or something

title: Conditional self-service actions
description:
Using the online demo as an example, there is currently a self-service action named "Add/Remove Service from Favorites". In my head, the ability to make an action conditionally available (based on one of more properties of the selected entity) would allow "Add Favorite" as an action for services that were not yet a favorite for me - while "Remove Favorite" would only be available for services that were already my favorite (this same thought process could be applied to the existing actions "Unlock Service" and "Lock Service"). 

Similarly (and maybe more compelling), an action like "Deploy Service" might only be available once certain criteria are met (an extension of sorts to the concept of scorecarding). Again referencing the demo service catalog, I could also see additional actions based on a distinguishing property like "Language" - maybe in our environment Python is managed distinctly different from React, and as such only certain actions would make sense in each context.

(There is also [this feature request](https://roadmap.getport.io/ideas/p/abilty-to-add-a-filter-so-only-certain-self-service-actions-appear-on-a-catalog) which also feels related...but not entirely overlapping.)

title: Support Additional Characters in Entity Identifier Regex Pattern
description:
We are using a self-service action in our Developer Portal to submit feedback, which creates or updates an entity using a title-based identifier. We've encountered an issue where the entity creation fails if the title includes certain characters, such as apostrophes (e.g., “can’t”).

We understand that Port enforces a regex pattern for entity identifiers:

^[A-Za-z0-9@_.+: \ \/=-]+

We would like to request support for additional characters (e.g., apostrophes ') in entity identifiers. This would enable a more natural feedback experience for users who may enter standard punctuation in form fields.

title: Improve webhook data source editor
description:
There are several improvements that could be made to this view. First, making the modal full screen would be a big step forward. Second, the test mapping feature seems broken or incomplete. It doesn’t properly evaluate filters, which causes errors on maps that would normally succeed. This happens because it runs JQ that should be skipped due to the filters. Additionally, more complex combinator search queries aren't evaluated in the test mapping view. 

Because of this, we often have to test by mapping a real entity and checking the audit log. When debugging failed maps in the audit log, we can’t see the original payload, only the mapping result is shown.

It would be really helpful if we could take any item from the audit log and load it into the test event window. Right now, we can only load the latest event, which means we have to guess what the broken state was, try to recreate it, and then quickly grab that latest event before anything else comes in.

title: Support secrets on webhook security configuration
description:
When using the Custom Integration: Webhook feature (https://docs.port.io/build-your-software-catalog/custom-integration/webhook/) we have the option of specifying a secret - i.e. for inbound request signature verification.

The "secret" value is directly input to the webhook settings screen.

When creating a webhook via IaC (e.g. `port_webhook` resource in Terraform), the secret is exposed in source code!

It would improve security if there was support for Port secrets here - i.e. the "secret" value references a secret, rather than having the raw secret value.

title: Create/update entity invocation type
description:
