The new "Create/update entity" invocation type for self-service actions and automations will allow updating catalog entities as part of a self-service action form/automation execution

For example, creating a specific self-service form for updating the Service team and Tier directly in the catalog.

title: GHA Invocation Error Improvements
description:
If any of the following are incorrect, then Port returns this error for Github Action invocation: "Got 404 while addressing github api, repo or workflow not found"

org name, repo name, workflow file name, or branch name (if using the "ref" key)

If would be helpful if this error provided more detailed information so that you did not have to perform trial and error changes to narrow it down.

Additionally, in some other failure scenarios, similar error messages can get cut off in the UI and they have to be copied over to notepad to be read. It would be quicker if Port could display the full message.

title: Provide complete swagger for api invocation
description:
Currently https://api.getport.io/swagger provides Schemas only for the API Requests.

Schemas for API Responses are missing.

It would be very helpful for those integrating the Port API to have a complete swagger file so they can auto-generate client code (for example via https://swagger.io/tools/swagger-codegen/)

title: Allow any selected entity's properties in the payload
description: On the user form, we are able to send from a selection of filtered entities. The self-service engineer should be able to choose which entity properties or property are relevant to send to the self-service action.

title: Controlling the payload - Map current entity
description:
As an extension to https://roadmap.getport.io/ideas/p/self-service-actions-controlling-the-payload,

It would be nice to have access to the entity the action is invoked on, and use JQ to map properties from the entity to the payload.

title: Enable referencing previous automation outputs (shared run context) + increase payload limits for chained automations
description:
Chained automations that depend on outputs from earlier steps currently require passing the full accumulated payload forward, which makes the payload grow exponentially and hits the payload limit. 

- add a better context-passing mechanism so downstream automations can reuse variables from prior steps without embedding full outputs (e.g., references to prior step outputs, a shared execution context/lightweight variable store scoped) to the automation run, and/or the ability to selectively pass only specific fields. 

- Increasing the max payload size AND

- reusable upstream context without payload bloat.

title: Dynamic permissions for self-service actions
description:
Ability to assign permissions according to the data model you defined for your organization.

How it will work:

When assigning permission (for example, to execute an action), the new capability will allow to query the catalog entities and create a permission condition based on the queries.

For example:

1. Allowing a developer to execute the "Deploy" action only if the developer is related to the same domain as the service

2. Allowing  a user to execute the "Lock/unlock deployments" action only if the user appears in the catalog as the "team leader" of that service

The first version will support assigning dynamic permission for executing an action, in the future we will add the support for editing entities.

title: Specify approval emails via dynamic permissions
description: Currently it is possible to configure an action to dynamically determine whether a user has a right to approve. However when the action is approved, all possible approvers are sent an email even those who were not eligible to approve the action. Ideally there would be a way to use dynamic permissions to specify who approval emails are sent to.

title: Manual approvals | Support requiring multiple approvals
Cancel approval step when there are no approvers
description:
Currently, when there are no approvers as a result of dynamic approvers calculation, the action moves to “waiting for approval,” but the approval is not sent to anyone. 

Add an option to decide whether an empty approvers list means no approval is required or the action is blocked

title: Ability to action stream logs real-time
description: Implement a functionality that streams logs to the user interface in real-time. This will enable users to monitor activities as they happen, without any delay. Currently, users must wait for an action to complete or a certain amount of data to be processed before logs can be viewed. This delay hinders real-time monitoring and troubleshooting.

title: MCP server usage logs
description:
the usage records of how the MCP is used:

- Total Tool API Calls (Daily)

- Calls per Active Client

- Unique Tools Used

- Most Used Tools

- What tools are accessed with what inputs / outputs

- - what types of blueprints and properties are being accessed

- - what skills are discovered through Port (or any other blueprint/catalog as needed).

- Active MCP Clients (Daily/Weekly)

- Total MCP Connections

title: Safe Execution for Concurrent Automation Runs
description:
Currently, automations that need to update or create multiple entities dynamically rely on the migration endpoint with filters, which can fail when concurrent runs overlap on the same blueprint.

A more reliable approach would be to enhance the UPSERT API to support dynamic, filter-based updates, allowing automations to update or create all entities that match a filter in a single atomic operation.

title: Support Service Account Credentials for Signing Port Execution Agent Messages
description:
Currently, the Port Execution Agent verifies incoming events by validating the X-Port-Signature header, which is signed using the organization-level Client Secret. This means that even when a service account is configured as the agent's credentials, the signature verification still relies on the org-level secret — not the service account credentials.

This creates a security concern for customers with strict internal security standards, who prefer to use service account credentials to limit blast radius in case of a credential leak, following the principle of least privilege.

title: Add live events to the integrations event log
Data extraction configuration
description:
Currently:

Data extraction configuration such as selecting which kinds to extract and defining API level selectors is set in the mapping. This means that the first sync after installing the integration includes only the default kinds and no selectors. The extraction behavior changes only after a user updates the mapping.

Expected:

We would like to move all configuration related to the extraction phase from the mapping to the installation and settings pages. This would allow users to filter data and choose kinds from the API even during the initial installation. It would also improve discoverability of available kinds and filters. This change is also required for the new architecture of the upcoming mapping experience planned for Q1.

title: Enhance `sendRawDataExamples` options for faster data source mapping
description:
For some kinds available in integration, the API responses can vary greatly depending on certain conditions. As a concrete example, in the github integration, the `branch` kind only contains properties like `.branch.commit.commit.author` when the branch is the default branch of a given repository, and in my mapping I set the query to `.branch.name == .repository.default_branch` to ensure I have access to that value.

What I'm currently finding is that the sendRawDataExamples option in integrations does not respect this query setting, so the ~5 examples retained from the api call might not even contain a valid api response (as in, one that passes the check in `query`). 

I have a few varied suggestions here:

- Allow `sendRawDataExamples` to respect the given query in a mapping.

- Allow `sendRawDataExamples` to have it's own query for stricter or looser example api responses.

- Allow independent resync of `sendRawDataExamples` separate from a resync of the data source.

Giving builders the ability to have stronger control over the examples defined in the data source view would significantly improve iteration time when dealing with complex mappings across multiple data sources.

title: Support AWS ElastiCache (not severless type)
description:
There are two types of AWS ElastiCache: serverless and non-serverless.

We use a lot of non-serverless ElastiCache, and we need to integrate its resources.

title: Audit Log (Runs tab) — Add Approver field and filtering
description:
Description: Currently, the Runs tab in the audit log does not expose approver details as a filterable column. It would be very useful to:

Display the assigned approvers and who actually approved a run as columns in the Runs table

Allow filtering by approver directly in the UI, without needing to query the API (GET /v1/actions/runs/:run_id/approvers) for each run individually

This would improve traceability and auditing of approval workflows significantly.

title: Native Slack approve/reject actions for self-service workflow approvals
description:
Desired outcome

The Port Slack app should natively notify the designated approver and surface inline Approve and Reject action buttons directly within the Slack message — no redirect required. The approval request should include the relevant context (requester, action, parameters) so the approver can make an informed decision without leaving Slack.

Why this matters

For an IDP platform focused on developer experience, inline approval actions in Slack are table stakes. Requiring approvers to leave Slack and navigate to Port adds friction, slows down approval cycles, and reduces adoption of self-service workflows. This is a foundational expectation for any approvals feature.

Freshdesk

Displays approval requests in Slack with a structured list of pending items and inline action buttons to approve or reject without leaving the conversation.

Sawmills

An example from a small startup demonstrating that inline Slack action buttons are achievable even at an early stage — reinforcing that this is an expected baseline, not a complex feature.

title: Ability to Rate Limit the number of workflow invocations
description: During a bulk import of entities, a workflow that triggers on ENTITY_CREATED was accidentally triggered causing 1k+ invocations of the workflow and subsequent AI nodes, this was a costly incident and we would like the ability to circuit break workflows when they attempt to run a certain number, or at least be able to stagger them so that 1k invocations are not all triggered concurrently.

title: Admin Override Toggle for Workflow Approvals
description:
Description: > Add an "Admin Override" toggle to the core approval settings for Self-Service Actions (SSA) and workflows.

Key Capability: > Allows Port Admins to intervene and instantly approve any pending request manually. When the override is used, it skips all remaining approvals in the sequence and immediately marks the workflow as approved.

title: Support team Ownership Field on POST /v1/workflows
description:
The team field is silently ignored when included in a POST /v1/workflows request body, making it impossible to assign team ownership to a workflow at creation time via the API. This is a confirmed feature gap, team is not currently a supported top-level field on the Workflows API, even though ownership can be set manually via the UI. 

Support the team field on POST /v1/workflows and PUT /v1/workflows/:id, consistent with how team works when upserting catalog entities.

Document the team field explicitly in the API reference.

title: Expose GitHub Node Conclusion in Workflow JQ Context
description:
After a GitHub Actions node runs, downstream nodes cannot access its conclusion. While the workflow run API exposes result: FAILED on the node run object, the .outputs available to downstream JQ expressions only include workflowRunUrl and workflowRunId, not result, workflowStatus, or any error detail.

This creates a dead end: the information exists in Port's data model, but it's not reachable from within the workflow itself.

result, workflowStatus, and error should be surfaced in .outputs["<node_id>"]

title: Sensitive output masking / redaction flag for workflow node variables
description:
When a workflow webhook node retrieves a dynamic credential (e.g., an OAuth access token) at runtime, the full response including the token is stored in variables.outputs and is permanently visible in the workflow run history UI for up to 90 days. There is currently no way to mark a variable as sensitive so that its value is redacted or masked in the run history display.

This is a security concern for any workflow that must fetch short-lived credentials dynamically, as Port Secrets (the recommended alternative) only support static, non-expiring values.

title: Add the ability to mark run as success/fail for create/update just like it is when using kafka topic
description:
We used Kafka for the backend until now.

There, a run is created in "In Progress" status and we mark it as success/fail according to the execution result.

I would like to have the same ability just with create/update invocation type.

title: Include stable action_id in GET Action Runs API
description: Exposing the stable action_id in the action runs response will ensure long-term data consistency and reliable analytics.

title: Terraform/Pulumi - Add workflow resource
description:
Add first-class `port_workflow` (or equivalent) resource to both the Terraform provider and the Pulumi package, so that `Workflows` can be defined, versioned, and managed as code, consistent with how Actions and Automations are handled today.

This is important for teams managing Port entirely through IaC (Terraform/Pulumi), as it removes the gap where workflows must be managed via the UI while everything else is code-managed.

title: Dynamic Permission policies as Policies Entities
description: The ability to reference a permission policy instead of rewriting - reusage for SSA , Blueprints and possibly automations

title: Implementing RBAC for API Requests.
description:
Hello PORT Team,

We have a case where our component, Octopus, is accessed by PORT via an API.

Since this is an external request, we are required to implement RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), meaning that every request must generate a JWT.

Practically, what we need is to perform a request to obtain the JWT before each SSA action and then include it in the header of the action.

title: Page-level permission scoping for Admin users
description:
Today, Admins bypass page-level read restrictions unconditionally — they always see all pages in the sidebar regardless of the read permissions set via PATCH /v1/pages/:id/permissions. There's no way to restrict which pages an Admin can access through a more dynamic permission model.

The request is to support page-level permission scoping for Admin users, similar to how blueprint permissions can be configured more granularly — so Admins can be intentionally excluded from specific pages rather than having blanket access to all of them.

title: To enable RBAC on SSA run pages
description:
Currently, a user can view the action run pages of actions that run on entities they are not permitted to access, or actions with entities as inputs, which they are not allowed to access. In the latter case, they can even view full details of the entity from the action run page. This violates the ownership defined on Port.

So, this feature request is to enable RBAC on action run pages.

title: Allow ocean integrations to run with granular permissions
description: Now Ocean integrations can run with service accounts, but they still require Admin role. We need the ability to scope the permissions for the ocean integration service account to read/register/update/delete only certain blueprints.

title: Audit Log Support for Permission Changes via Terraform
description:
Currently, permission changes made through Terraform are not captured in the audit logs

The request is to add support for logging permission changes triggered via Terraform in the audit logs

title: Custom permissions to view/edit action runs
description: We would like to be able to edit action runs with service accounts, without the need to make them Admins.

title: Import RBAC from Datadog to Port
description: Datadog has a very robust and complex RBAC we are using to ensure that users only see what is relevant to them. We want to have Datadog continue to be the source of truth for this and import the RBAC to have Port users only be able to see the data they see in Datadog and nothing more.

title: Order self-service action items in the blueprint
description: We would like to have an ability for ordering self-service action items coming from the blueprint.

title: Catalog pages as a widget
description: Option to create catalog pages as widget similar like recently used actions.The goal is to make it easier for users to navigate to new custom pages and improve the overall user experience.

title: Improve default Catalog properties
description:
Today by default when installing an integration we see 3 properties: title, created at, updated at. This requires the end user to spend time for every single integration to show/view the required properties. 

Integrations should come with a default best practice view to reduce this manual time

title: Action auto generated input based on previous inputs: option to disable from editing
Hyperlink in Action input titles
description: You can create hyperlinks in descriptions using the [text](link) syntax. It would be useful if you could do the same on Titles for action inputs instead of making users hover over the description.

title: Improve readability of action inputs in approval UI
description:
Action inputs currently appear as raw JSON in the Port UI.

The request is to enhance the Port UI to display action inputs in a similarly human-readable, structured format

title: Support for enumLabels in self-service action inputs
description:
Feature: Support for enumLabels in self-service action inputs

Use Case: Ability to show user-friendly display labels while passing technical keys/values to the backend

Example:

"enum": ["prod", "stg", "dev"],

"enumLabels": {

  "prod": "Production Environment",

  "stg": "Staging Environment", 

  "dev": "Development Environment"

}

Benefit: Improves UX by separating what users see from what the backend processes

title: Ability to Hide the “Execute” Button in Self-Service Action Forms
description: We’d like to request the ability to hide the Execute button in self-service action forms via a configuration parameter (e.g., `hideExecuteButton`). Currently, the button is always displayed, even for forms intended purely for informational or navigational purposes, which can confuse users and limits UI flexibility.

title: Increase self-service action form size for survey-based actions
description: When the self-service action is used as a survey, the current form size limits clarity and ease of response. Enlarging the form would provide a more spacious layout, making it easier for respondents to view and answer survey questions comfortably.

title: Add direct link to entities in dropdown list items
description:
When users select entities from dropdown lists, they often need to navigate directly to that entity's detailed view. Currently, there's no quick way to do this from the dropdown itself, which can lead to extra steps and time spent searching for the entity.

We propose adding a direct link (e.g., a small arrow or text link) next to each dropdown list item, allowing users to quickly open the detailed view of the selected entity without leaving their current workflow. This functionality is based on the design shown in the attached prototype.

title: Default value enums not populating
description: If I create an enum with a default value (pic 1) then I expect the default value to be populated and visible in entity pages. However it's blank (pic 2). I've tried re-ingesting entities but there's no change.

title: Default value for timer property
description: Ability to define a calculation default value for timer property type based on the creation timestamp of the entity.  It would be nice for example assign a default value of now()+X hours

title: GitOps dry run - Support custom validations
description:
For the GitHub checks in the GitHub app for file kind, 

some scenarios are not being handled by Port API:

1) When the identifier is null, Port auto-generates an identifier with a UUID so no error is raised from Port API, even though we want to enforce it

2) When you want each field in the yaml to fit to a property in Port, 1:1, and use all the data of the file. That is when you want any typo in the yaml keys to raise an error

3) For a scenario where you want Port to make sure all the properties of the entity are mapped, and null for a property is not expected (instead of making fields required)

title: Support for Live Regex Validation in String Inputs
description: Regex validation used to run live for string inputs, which was a much better experience than waiting until action execution. We’d like to have live validation back, or a setting to toggle it on/off.

title: Test mapping - adding more validations
description:
Currently, the "Test mapping" in the data source mapping validates only JQ issues.

We would like to add more validation such as:

"Blueprint doesn't exist"

"Property doesn't  exist"

"Property is invalid" (wrong type, wrong value for enum)

etc.

title: UI Filtering with JQ on Object Fields
description:
It would be helpful to include some type of interface, perhaps JQ expression, for consumers to filter a catalog view based on a complex object JSON field. This is possible in creating new catalogs with filter expressions for Admins, but not for consumers who wish to filter by the object.

There are two scenarios below to help indicate benefit:

1. We have our CI/CD pipelines stored as objects that enable us to detect what types of things people are doing in their pipelines, using certain actions/tasks, using base workflows, etc. We pull out some of this into calculated fields. We need to search adhoc by some additional actions/tasks, and other than a developer manually going through all the pipelines (3000) in source control, they could easily query with jq the definitions and filter to pipelines using some of the feature they are thinking about making breaking contract changes too (many use cases on why you'd want to identify impact to pipelines).

2. Similar scenario with objects in the API space, where we can identify API specs (Stored as OpenAPI) using certain models, notation or constructs and filter it down.

title: regex support in search query rules / mapping relations
description:
The ability to use substring or regex matching inside Port’s search rules, especially when the target property is an array of strings (such as tags).

This could be via:

- a dedicated operator like containsSubstring / matches, or

- allowing regex patterns in value (e.g. ^service:{{serviceTitle}}).

{

  "property": "tags",

  "operator": "matches",      // or similar

  "value": ".*{{ .event.diff.after.title }}.*"

}

title: Action API viewable per action
description: The builder data sources has this really wonderful code view where you can see the blueprint API entirely with a working example. It would be really nice if you could go into a self service action and see a similar view.

title: Support team search on Ocean and Webhook integrations
description: Port's API support the mapping of direct ownership in the form of search query. This request is to implement support in the Ocean's framework and the generic Webhook integration.

title: Ability to limit the LLM/AI invocations per user
description: Right now the limit for AI invocations are organization based, we would need to be able to set consumption/invocation limits per user

title: Port AI Invocation API Supports Passing User Context
description: When integrating with Port Agents via API, it would be helpful to be able to pass in the context of a request for a particular user. In general, there should be a mechanism to allow authorization as a particular user from a third party system to enable building custom integrations. Our use case is specifically related to SSO-based auth as well.

title: Allow toggle of conditions array in dynamic permission from OR to AND
description:
Currently each condition in a dynamic self service action permission is evaluated with an implicit OR between them.

So a policy can have two conditions and will allow execution if only one is met. You can force an AND by building a JQ expression and putting all the logic inside of a single condition, but this is rather complex and most customers won't know how to do this.

Having the ability to change the behavior from OR to AND as needed would make this a lot easier for customers.

title: Approvers list in the approve notification
description:
Currently, when triggering a self service action with manual approval required via webhook, the notification that is sent to the webhook is limited with data.

Having the list of users who can approve the action allows you to create a backend that acts upon the approval notifications that are sent out.

title: Display action list when hovering over action icon
description: On catalog pages there is an action icon (lightning bolt) next to entities that lets you invoke actions directly from the table. Currently you have to click twice, once to open the list and once to select the action. It would be nice to remove a click by displaying the action list when hovering over the icon.

title: Custom timestamps in action run logs
description: We want to change the system-generated timestamp that Port assigns to each log entry to a custom timestamp we manually specify in the action run log stream window.

title: Action runs | Automatic logs sending / from file
description: Instead of requiring a dedicated API call done by the user

title: Provide OpenTelemetry metrics & logs
description: As a platform engineer responsible for our Port infrastructure, I want to consume operational metrics and log data using an open format within my standard observability platform so that I can effectively measure self-service workflows, dashboard usage, event triggers, web hooks, data source sync jobs, and so on. Log data for sync jobs and system auditing should also be available via the same standard observability pipeline.

title: Configurable Retry Status Codes for Integrations
description:
Summary: 

- Allow users to configure which HTTP status codes trigger automatic retries via spec.yaml, without modifying integration source code.

Background: 

- The Ocean framework's RetryConfig class already supports additional_retry_status_codes, but this is not exposed to users. All integrations that use custom retry codes (PagerDuty, Sentry, GitHub, etc.) have them hardcoded in the client code. 

- Default retryable status codes: 400, 401, 429, 502, 503, 504

Problem: 

- Different third-party APIs have varying reliability characteristics. Some APIs intermittently return 500 or other error codes that would benefit from retry logic. Users currently cannot configure this without forking and maintaining a custom version of the integration.

Proposed Solution: 

- Add an optional additionalRetryStatusCodes configuration to spec.yaml.

Benefits

- Users can adapt to their specific API behavior without code changes

- Fully backward compatible as an optional configuration

- Leverages existing RetryConfig infrastructure

Use Cases

- GitLab self-hosted instances returning intermittent 500 errors under load

- APIs behind flaky proxies returning frequent 502/503 errors

description:
Improve export/import reliability, environment promotion, and multi-org migration to prevent rollout delays and support enterprise adoption.

especially the native terraform tooling

title: gitlab pipeline trigger action
description: The list of statuses is currently a closed list containing only (Success and Failure) As we understand, the status field should reflect the Pipeline status, in this case the list should contain all Gitlab's possible pipeline statuses: (created, waiting_for_resource, preparing, pending, running, success, failed, canceled, skipped, manual, scheduled)

title: Add support for AWS::RDS::DBCluster in AWS v3 integration
description:
Request to add first-class support for the AWS::RDS::DBCluster resource type to the AWS v3 integration so ElastiCache clusters can be ingested as their own kind and mapped into Port blueprints.

The feature should expose key ElastiCache cluster attributes so they can be mapped into a dedicated blueprint and used for catalog relationships and scorecards.

title: Delete entities per kind
description:
Today the deletion phase in resyncs is cross all kinds, which means that if one kind fails, deletion is aborted. this causes irrelevant entities in the Portal.

We'd like to change the deletion behavior in resync so each kind performs it's own deletion.

title: Entity and user/team pickers should allow dynamic filters and defaults
Allow dynamic value for ActionButton Text
description: Can we allow dynamic value using jqqyery for executeActionButtonText field, so that the button text can change based on previous selection.

title: Base64 encoding function within SSAs
description:
Add support for a dedicated native Base64 encoding function within SSAs.

If your backend uses Basic Auth, base64 encoding username:PAT (or :PAT) is the correct approach, and right now you have to do so outside of Port.

title: Enforce UI-Level Input Validations at the Backend/API Level for Self-Service Actions/Workflows
description:
Input-level dataset filters and required field validations in Self-Service Actions are currently UI-side only. Any execution path that bypasses the form UI, JSON mode, direct API calls, or Port's MCP, skips these validations entirely, allowing invalid or unauthorized inputs to be submitted. 

The desired behavior is for all execution paths to respect the same validation rules defined in the form UI, with meaningful error messages returned on violation. Current workarounds are insufficient for all cases:

Dynamic permissions: server-side enforcement, but requires manual policy configuration per action.

ownedByTeam: true on blueprint read permissions, restricts entity visibility at the catalog level, but does not cover all use cases.

title: Give Input node approvers a focused decision view instead of the full workflow graph
description:
When a user opens a run specifically to respond to a pending Input node, show a simplified, scoped view by default - just that node's description, form fields, and buttons - similar to the old Actions approval model. The full graph could still be available behind a "view full workflow" link for technical users/admins who want the context, but it shouldn't be the default landing experience for someone who just needs to approve or decline.

This would make Input nodes a viable replacement for Actions' requiredApproval in organizations that have non-technical approvers in the loop, which is a common case for access-governance and change-approval use cases.

title: Improve Visibility of Run Status Changes in Audit Logs
description:
Currently, when a workflow or action run's status is updated (e.g., marked as failed or succeeded), it is not clearly visible who or what made that change, whether it was the integration, the Port actions backend, or a user manually patching the run.

Surface more visibly in the run page and/or audit logs what entity (user, integration, or system) last changed the run status, including the specific action taken.

Consider adding audit log entries for run status changes, including the actor (user identity or integration user-agent) and the type of change made.

title: Disable workflow execute button while execution is in progress
description:
Currently, when a workflow is triggered, the execute button remains enabled. If the workflow takes time to start, users can click the button multiple times, unintentionally triggering duplicate executions.

The execute button should be disabled (greyed out) immediately after the first click and remain disabled until the workflow reaches a terminal state (SUCCESS, FAILURE, or DECLINED), preventing accidental multiple executions.

Users may unknowingly trigger the same workflow several times in quick succession, leading to duplicate runs and unexpected results.

title: Event trigger for ALL self-service actions
description: I want to be able to trigger an automation or workflow for any self-service action. Currently you can trigger an automation for a self-service action, but it's tied to a specific action rather than ALL actions.

title: https://status.port.io/ incidents automaticically set org announcement banner
description:
I'm using Port's newly released announcement capability to manually notify users of Port's ongoing incident. It would be nice to optionally be able have these announcements automatically set/removed during an incident.

https://status.port.io/

title: Dynamic approvers test JQ
description:
Adding a test JQ window in dynamic approvers window, just like in the automation trigger window.

This will allow a user to test the conditions and get a list of approvers (users) to improve visibility and reduce mystery around dynamic approvers list behavior.

title: Multi-Step Action Visibility
description:
Current State

- Complex actions run as a single opaque execution. - Limited visibility into intermediate progress or where

failures occur.

Requested Capability

- GitHub Actions–style granular step visibility for complex workflows. - Example step breakdown:

terraform plan → terraform apply → tests → validation . - Real-time status updates and step-

level logs.

Customer Context

- Connor requested “visibility into multi-step action progress.” - Port mentioned a “CI/CD visualization”

feature is on the roadmap.

Business Impact

- Faster debugging and incident response. - Higher trust in automation and improved reliability perception.

title: Create a page to view the history of permissions granted to the user
description:
From a security perspective, it is necessary to be able to store and retrieve the history of permissions granted to users.

This ticket suggests creating a page in tools like Audit Log or Mixpanel where we can see the history of a user's permission changes.

title: Default port team with all users
description: In cases where an admin needs to perform actions for all users in Port, such as sending announcements, having a team that includes everyone would be incredibly useful. However, creating this manually means that each time a new user signs up, the admin would need to add them manually. To streamline this process, it would be necessary to have a default team that automatically contains all users.

title: Retrieve via API ownership information for a user
description: Currently the "Get a user" API endpoint (https://docs.getport.io/api-reference/get-a-user)  only returns basic information about a user (see the image below taken from a live demo environment). It would be good to have an ability to also retrieve ownership data. This could be useful to automate users management depending upon whether they are mentioned somewhere in entities or not.

title: Register Permission Should Allow Populating Properties for Member users
description: Users with entity register permission should be able to fill all blueprint fields during creation without requiring additional updateProperties permissions.

title: Audit log for individual fields
description: Often I want to see when and by what a specific field was changed on an entity. The problem is we have some entities with hundreds or thousands of edits in the log. Tracking down the specific edit that changed that field last can be difficult. It would be really nice to see a breakdown of each of the edits to the entity that involved that specific field.

title: Show triggering user in audit logs for entities created via self-service actions
description:
Problem

When a self-service action creates another entity, the audit log shows the entity as being created by Port automation. While the action run itself contains the triggering user’s information, that context is not surfaced in the audit log.

This makes it difficult to:

- Trace ownership and accountability

- Understand who initiated changes when reviewing audit logs

- investigate issues without jumping between audit logs and action runs

Current behavior

- Audit log entry:  Type “Port automation”

- Triggering user is only visible in the self-service action run details

Expected behavior

Audit logs should display the user who triggered the self-service action as the creator of any entities created by that action (or at least include them as additional context, e.g. “Created by Port automation (triggered by [USER])”).

title: Ability to select timeframe in the event log
description: It would be helpful to be able to select a timeframe for logs in the exporter event log. Also, a copy button would be useful here.

title: Azure Live logs
description:
Request to have a feature where Azure Entities that support live logs can be seen from inside port. 

Intent is to help ensure that when one visits the entity page, live logs of a resource appear only upon user visit action to the live logs tab under the entity

title: Increase webhook integration audit log event count
description: Currently the audit logs for webhook integrations only shows the last event. This is a major limitation when attempting to troubleshoot since different event types have varying data structures, making a single event insufficient.

title: Integration  "event catalog" https://www.eventcatalog.dev
description:
support an integration just like backstage https://www.eventcatalog.dev/integrations/backstage

"This plugin allows you to import your EventCatalog directly into Backstage. Get EventCatalog features, visualisations and more directly in Backstage."

title: Search Markdown on Catalog Page
description: Currently you can search the contents of markdown properties using the global search in the "Tech Docs" tab. You should also be able to search the contents of markdown properties in the catalog page search.

title: Hide actions from entity menu
description:
Currently, Actions are tied to a Blueprint, and will offer all Actions for each Entity in the Catalog menu.

Having the option to hide Actions on specific Entities will allow to clean up the catalog, and disable Actions on entities that should not run it.

title: Make actions log user friendly
description:
One of the most used parts of the portal is the actions.

The logs presented today are completely raw which reduces the usability of the actions in particular and, overall, of the entire portal.

The issues that a raw log presents:

* There is no way to distinguish technical logs (like agent logs) from backend generated

* Warnings, important information to the users generated by the action are not identifiable (e.g. with icon)

* Links, if provided, are not clickable.

I would suggest replacing the textbox with a dynamic table in the lines of the attachment:

title: MCP Action Access Controls - Restrict Actions by Invocation Source
description:
Currently, permissions are scoped to users and roles, but there is no way to restrict an action to specific invocation channels (e.g., UI only vs. MCP). This is a concern for high-risk operations such as production deployments, where teams want the additional guardrails and visibility that the Port UI provides.

Relying on the Claude/MCP client config to restrict actions is fragile — it lives outside Port's governance model, isn't auditable in Port, and can be bypassed or misconfigured. Native support in Port ensures consistent enforcement across all MCP clients and aligns with existing RBAC patterns.

Adding an invocation source control at the action level in Port, allowing admins to configure which channels an action can be triggered from would allow teams to enforce that sensitive actions (e.g., prod deploys, destructive operations) cannot be triggered via MCP, without needing to rely on external configuration in the AI client (e.g., Claude system prompt restrictions).

title: Expose Action Form Trigger in Custom Widget/Plugin SDK
description: Add support for opening a self-service action form directly from a custom widget/plugin, without navigating to the Self-Service Actions tab

title: Dropdown list with a "insert string" option
description:
To have the ability to create an entity selection input with an input string to create a new entity. 

For example you could choose the repository from the catalog or create a new with the name you provided?

title: New input type - Map
description:
Support a new input of type map (ENUM object where you can select a key, but the payload will have the value).

Use case: I have some values in my backend that represent what kind of lambda function will be triggered. In the action, I would like to present the users with an easy to understand input that is more meaningful than the lambda token.

Example: The input will be an ENUM dropdown, that will represent a JSON object with multiple keys and values (Lambda's names and their matching tokens). The user will be offered a selection from the Lambdas names, and the input will have the selected lambda token).

Currently, this can be done using Control the Payload (I can have an if that checks the input and calculates the relevant value), but this is not maintainable when you have a lot of inputs.

title: Require Object type input property contents, not input itself
description:
Currently you can't require properties within an object type input in a self service action. You can require the input as a whole, or require a property type for the properties in the object, but that will only enforce type if they appear. It doesn't actually require the presence of the property. 

So, I don't want the entire object input to be required. I just want specified properties in the object to be required IF that input is used.

title: In self service section, allow for the installtionId  to be a computed value and not static value
description:
We’re using an INTEGRATION_ACTION with integrationProvider: "GITHUB" and would like to render installationId dynamically from the selected repository’s org_name:

"installationId": "{{ .inputs.repository.properties.org_name | ascii_downcase }}"

title: Placeholder value in self-service action fields
description:
When using regex to validate fields value we either have to not provide a default value or provide a valid value.

It would be useful to be able to set placeholder value to give user an example but forcing them to set a new value.

This prevent the case where the action is wrongly submitted with the example default value.

title: Add uiDefault to Prevent Validation on Initial Load
description: Add support for uiDefault option to apply default values at the UI level, preventing validation from triggering too soon during form initialization.

title: UI Cache Invalidation / Forced Dashboard Updates
description:
When changes are made to dashboards, widgets, scorecards, or other UI elements in Port, end users do not automatically receive the updated view. 

Currently:

- A hard refresh (or clearing browser history/cache) is required to see new changes.

- A soft refresh is sometimes insufficient

Proposed Solution (from [USER])

A config/version check or ETag-based mechanism that busts the locally cached view whenever a dashboard, widget, or scorecard is changed on the backend. This would ensure users automatically receive the latest UI state without manual intervention.

title: Widget conditional display
description: We would like to be able to add conditions on widgets. For example if the number is below our threshold, it should be red. Otherwise green. And maybe even send an alert if red.

title: jq implementation inconsistency between exporters and webhooks
description:
As a part of our integration strategy, we are opting to use webhooks for real-time data ingestion, and then coming along behind on a scheduled interval for a more complete sync (to ensure that we cover for any misses in the webhook process). 

The first image is the jq mapping for cleaning up the branch name for the scheduled sync (note the lack of needing to escape the double quotes in the jq `gsub` function call - attempting to escape them will actually cause errors).

The second image is a similar jq mapping for cleaning up the branch name for the incoming webhook (real-time) data (note needing to escape the double quotes in the jq `gsub` function call - attempting to not escape them will cause errors).

I would have expected that the syntax should be consistent across data source types?

description:
Add Ability to filter relations with JQ.

From example, i want to be able to related repo to other repo that has specific property(library)

title: Expose Richer Executing User Context in SSA Backend
description:
The SSA backend currently exposes only a limited, trusted subset of the executing user’s data, while the User Form provides a richer payload. Passing the User Form .user object to the backend is not safe, as it can be spoofed and allow user impersonation.

This idea is to expose additional trusted context about the executing user (such as team relationships) directly in the SSA backend payload, without relying on user-provided inputs.

title: Port Secrets Support in Webhook Security Configuration

Allow the {{ .secrets.<secret_name> }} syntax in the secret field for webhook, consistent with how secrets are already used in self-service action and automation payloads.

"security": {

title: Use webhooks to trigger Code Coverage and Test Run kinds for ADO
description: Currently we grab ADO Code Coverage and Test Run results as a part of a sync. As these kinds typically created when a Pipeline Run occurs, we could use the "live event" webhooks from ADO for pipeline runs to call the Code Coverage and Test Run endpoints rather than sync. This would speed up the overall ADO syncs, reduce the change of rate limiting and also provide near-real time data for Code Coverage and Test Runs, inline with the pipeline runs. So when a pipeline run is completed, we should then call the Code Coverage and Test Run endpoints to provide the additional metadata.

title: Add teamsIdentifier, and teams to user object in Self Service Action Dynamic Permissions
description:
Currently the teamsIdentifier, and teams arrays are not available in the user context in Self Service action dynamic permissions.

For example, if you want to use "{{.user.teamsIdentifier}}" or "{{.user.teams[].name}}" as a value in a dynamic permissions policy, you can't do that as those values aren't present on the .user object in the dynamic permissions/self service action context.

title: Allow the configuring of action permissions to allow organization generated tokens to trigger actions
Apply permissions to entity selection inputs in Actions
description: Currently action permissions only restrict Day-2 and Delete target entities so that people who don't have read access cannot select those entities. The permissions should also apply to entity selection inputs.

title: Enable action execution permissions based on user data
description: Introduce configurable permissions that allow actions to be executed based on specific user data. For example, restrict actions to the current on-call user or to a user who provided a particular answer in a survey. This feature would ensure that actions are performed only by the appropriate users as defined by dynamic criteria.

title: Manual Approval by owner
description: Add the ability to allow approval by owner, allowing more flexibility in the permissions

title: Approver's Dashboard
description: As an approver, I would like to have an intuitive dashboard that allows me to efficiently manage my approval requests. This dashboard should display all the requests in my queue, provide access to the history of past approvals, and offer advanced filtering options to easily focus on those "Waiting for Approval." Additionally, I would like the capability to approve/reject multiple requests simultaneously through a bulk approval feature.

title: Show full action description in action card
description:
When an action title or description is longer than the available space for the card, there is no way to see the full text. When displaying the actions on the actual Self-service page, any overflow text is indicated by an ellipsis and then available to see in a tooltip via hovering over the text with your mouse.

Self-service page: (see larger screenshot)

Action card on a dashboard page: (see smaller screenshot, this can also be seen on the demo "My Team's Scorecards" page - https://demo.getport.io/my_teams_scorecards - when on smaller screens)

Alternately, could the wrapping div be updated to no longer hide the overflow/truncate the text, and instead simply grow vertically based on the text presented?

title: Add action run status description
description: Currently action run status are predefined and limited to "Success", "Failure" and "In progress". This feature will add the option to provide additional descriptions next to the status and further explain the current step, like "waiting_for_resource", "preparing", "canceled", etc.

title: Clear action run notification badge
description: The new action runs view displays a notification badge counting the number of a user's "In progress" or "Waiting for approval" runs. It would be nice to have a button to manually clear the badge for runs you know will take a while to finish / be approved.

title: Export Action Run History
description: Currently Port does not have the ability to export action runs via the UI, only the API. It would be beneficial if an export button was added to the Runs History page similar to normal catalog pages.

title: Expose integration event logs via API or streaming
description: Currently to view integration event logs you must use the UI to view them. It would be great if these could be exposed via an API or via log streaming to allow for real time troubleshooting and/or analysis.

title: Configurable automatic execution of self-service actions from Slack
description:
Today, when a self-service action is initiated via the Port Slack app, the bot intentionally does not execute the action automatically. Instead, it collects some parameters and then redirects the user back to the Port UI to review and confirm the action. This behavior is by design for safety and control reasons, but some we would like the option to complete the full action flow directly in Slack without switching context. 

Requested Capability

Add a configuration option that allows admins to control whether self-service actions triggered via the Slack app can be:

Executed automatically from Slack once all required parameters are collected, or

Kept in the current “review in Port UI before execution” mode.

This could be exposed as a per-action flag (e.g., “Allow automatic execution from Slack”) or as an organization-level policy for Slack-initiated actions.

Value / Impact

Reduces context switching for developers and on-call engineers who want to complete workflows entirely within Slack.

Preserves safety by making automatic execution opt-in and configurable by platform/admin teams.

Aligns Slack app behavior with customers’ expectations for fully chat-native self-service while keeping the current secure default.

title: Forward everything the Port Execution Agent gets and make it transparent
description:
When using the Execution Agent, I would like to just set "enabled: false" in the 'control_the_payload_config.json' file and make it completely transparent. I mean for it to just forward whatever payload it receives: headers, body, etc.

Thank you.

title: “Execute” Button on the First Step of the Input Window
description:
We would like to have an “Execute” button to the first step of the Self-service action with many steps input window. This button will allow users to initiate the action immediately if they do not need to modify any fields in subsequent steps.

Rationale:

The first step contains all required fields for the action. For users who do not wish to change any optional fields in the following steps, this “Execute” button would allow them to bypass unnecessary navigation through all steps just to initiate the action at the end. This feature will improve user efficiency and reduce friction in workflows where default settings are frequently used.

Expected Behavior:

	•	Location: The “Execute” button should appear prominently on the first step of the input form.

	•	Functionality: If clicked, the button should validate all required fields in the first step, initiate the action

	•	Fallback: If any required fields are missing or incorrect, the button should provide feedback to the user, prompting them to complete or correct those fields.

Benefits:

	•	Saves time for users who don’t need to modify optional fields.

	•	Reduces the number of interactions needed for common use cases.

	•	Enhances overall user experience by streamlining the workflow.

title: Support for AWS::MemoryDB::User and AWS::MSK::ServerlessCluster in AWS V3 Integration
description:
Request to add support for the following AWS resource kinds in the AWS V3 integration:

AWS::MemoryDB::User

AWS::MSK::ServerlessCluster

These kinds are currently not supported in AWS V3 and were previously associated with issues in the old AWS integration, which is being deprecated. 

Our goal is to have these resources ingested into the Port catalog via the AWS V3 integration so we can manage and visualize them consistently with the rest of our AWS estate.

Please let us know if any additional details (properties, example ARNs, or use cases) are needed to prioritize or design this support.

Thank you!

title: Control which Port Execution Agent deployment process which message with polling streamer
description:
With Port Execution Agent that use polling streamer  (https://docs.port.io/actions-and-automations/setup-backend/webhook/port-execution-agent/usage#polling-streamer), messages are acknowledged before processing and cannot be claimed by another agent once fetched.

This allows multiple agents to run in parallel without conflicts, but requires using the same filtering logic across all agents to avoid unintended filtering.

You cannot control which agent processes which message at the moment.

Suggested solution:

Set and optional "cluster identifier" that is evaluated when executing the run. The poller will send its "cluster identifier", only matching runs will be fetched.

title: In port execution agent allow the agent to have SSL no-verify option when communicating with the remote server
description:
We want to have the option to have SSL no-verify in the port execution agent.

We want to communicate with an internal service without the hassle of handling the self signed certificates

title: To include errors/warnings related to the regex pattern of file path in kind "file" in the Audit log/Event Log
description: The GitHub app's Audit or Event logs do not warn or error when the file path's regex pattern is incorrect in kind "file". Adding the relevant error or warning will reduce the time it takes for the user to recognise the issue.

title: Search catalog pages
description: Search for catalog pages in the catalog menu, to enhance discoverability of available pages

title: Action Input Overrides During Manual Approval
description:
In some cases, a user will submit a self-service action that requires a manual approval step.

In a subset of those cases, it is possible that the admin that approves the request will want to make a change to the inputs provided by the user (for example, the user requested a DB with a node count of 3, and the admin is willing to approve the request but with a node count of 2).

This feature will give the admin the option to override the inputs provided by the user and approve the request with updated inputs.

title: Show input parameters in Action History Widget
description: The ability to display input parameters for a 2-day self-service action in the Action History widget. Now, you could add an input parameter to the widget, but it would appear empty.

title: User input: location
description: User inputs - I would like to have an option to search an address using 3rd provider like open street maps, or google maps (using api key) or something else. So the user input will be fill from this search auto complete

title: Copy raw value option
description:
When using Port’s UI, the table and specific entity views give users a quick copy value button. When performing the copy, the value copied to the clipboard will be the same one displayed in the web UI, which usually goes through some layers of HTML and JS interpolation, resolving things such as `\n` to actual HTML newlines etc.

For cases where the real format of the property value is important (for example a K8s kubeconfig) it would be helpful to have a “copy raw” option, making it possible to copy the kubeconfig as it is, with the newlines that were originally part of the kubeconfig. This makes it easy to take the real value and use it in a CI/CD workflow, or simply add it to an existing local kubeconfig managed by the kubectl CLI.

title: Terraform provider | Conditional page deletion capability
description: Introduce the ability to conditionally delete pages through the Terraform provider when managing blueprints, by specifying a deletion condition (e.g., true/false) within the Blueprint JSON file.

title: Reflect invalid JQ results to stakeholders
description:
Results of JQ could always be invalid in the context where they are used. This will show up in different parts of the app, such as action user inputs.

We should find a way to alert relevant stakeholders to the fact that the calculated value is invalid when it occurs.

title: Surface JQ errors
description:
Today, when there is an error with a JQ, you can't see it, and usually, the action is skipped.

In Integration Mapping, resources will not be created. In automations/actions, it won't run.

Ideally, JQ errors will appear somewhere you can monitor and act upon.

title: I want to search entities with regex
description: Whether in the global search, or searching within a table, I'd like to search using regular expressions to take advantage of known conventions or shapes to the data (e.g. starts with, optional characters, etc)

title: Entities example for backend playground
description:
Port actions backend have a playground that can be used for testing the JQ mapping. The examples that are being provided are automatically generated and in some cases are not aligned with the actual data.

By adding the option to add entities to the example section, users can validate the JQ correctly without the need to align the schema.

title: Add log to action run invocation method
description:
Add the option to use a generic invocation method that sends a log message to an action run ID provided as an input.

This will make it easier to send logs to actions in a generic and standardized way

title: Port agent - Control the payload through UI
description:
Currently, you can only update the mapping config directly at the agent/provide the mapping when you install it.

Having a way to edit it through the UI (like other integrations) will ease the usage and create a better experience.

title: Runs - displaying the payload
description: The payload of a specific run is now displayed in Port’s specific run page and audit log under the “Payload” property.

title: Disallow saving actions with no execute permissions
description:
Currently, execute permissions can be removed entirely, which allows an action to be saved with no execute permissions at all. We need a product safeguard to prevent this by either:

Disallowing actions from being saved without any execute permissions, or

Automatically retaining the Admin role as a default execute permission.

title: Manual approval for self-service actions
description:
Admins can define an approval step on chosen self-service actions.

 This capability will allow setting guardrails on sensitive actions, while still allowing users to perform actions in a self-service manner.

 Actions with an approval step will be created in “waiting for approval” status, the approving party will be notified so they can approve or decline the action.

 See [how to configure an approval step](https://docs.getport.io/self-service-actions/self-service-actions-deep-dive/#manual-approval)

title: Option to Exclude Hidden Inputs from SSA Manual-Approval Emails
description:
Hidden SSA inputs (configured via visibility rules) are still included in the default manual-approval email by design, to give approvers full context.

Request

Add a configuration option to exclude hidden inputs from the default approval email, while keeping them in the submitted payload for backend processing. For example, an action-level flag like excludeHiddenInputsFromApprovalEmail: true (default false to preserve current behavior).

Value

Reduces noise in approval emails (especially large JSON/object inputs).

Lets teams keep technical/auxiliary fields hidden from both requesters and approvers, without losing them from the action payload.

title: Bypass Self-Service Approval Need if submitter is an approver
description:
My team approves certain self-service actions. Me and my team also use the same self-service actions for our own day-to-day work at times. When we submit one of these requests we approve our own requests. While some requests might warrant a separate approver, even on the same team, in our case we don't. We simply need the self-service action to execute, but we have to approve our own request, which is just extra work.

Today there is a "General access" section at the bottom of the Approvers section of the Edit action window. There is a toggle for Admins, so admins do not need approval. My Feature Request is to possibly rename the "General access" heading because this doesn't seem intuitive. Instead, name it something like "Approval Bypass". Keep Admins and add a new toggle like "Approvers". When enabled, if a requestor is a named approver or in an approver group then requests by that user would not need to be approved.

title: Allow non-admins to create and/or edit self-service actions
description:
I want to allow some users to be able to create self-service actions in our STG environment without giving them full Admin access.

Alternatively, if we had RBAC over who can EDIT self-service actions then I could create a self-service action that creates a "shell" self-service action for users with the proper RBAC on it that would grant them edit access.

title: Action run dashboard/homepage widget
description:
A dashboard/homepage widget that displays the runs of a specific self-service action.

The widget will display as columns the general details of each run (ID, status, start, end) and also the specific inputs of the action inputted by the user who executed it.

title: Dynamic run name for an action run
description: I would like a new tab and property in the 'Action Runs' audit page, which is a dynamic title that can be created from the inputs and entity properties.

title: Execute another self-service action run with the similar inputs
description:
Today, after a run is completed, it is possible to run it again with the "Re-run" button, which opens the execution form with the run's inputs that can be edited.

We want the ability to execute another run with the same inputs as an existing run, while it is in progress.

We might need to change the wording from "Re-run" as it can be thought as if the current run would be cancelled.

And, to prevent running the same inputs twice by mistake, we might want to open a confirmation dialog.

title: Support Multi-Dimensional Arrays
description:
Currently Port supports Arrays of Strings, Numbers, and Objects. This Arrays are limited to one dimension only.

It could be useful to support multi-dimensional Arrays as well.

For example, a 2-dimensional Array of Strings could be used to contain tables with multiple rows and columns.

title: Agnostic automation triggers
description: Feature request down the line: automation triggers off of something a little more Port-agnostic like a message in a queue.  Similar to something like a Lambda function in AWS being invoked by SQS.

title: Automations | Show warning incase automation will be triggered over x times a day
description:
In case an automation which is about to be created is going to be triggered a lot of times, a warning for the customer is important, since it might cause a lot of pipelines and jobs to run, inflicting high costs.

Using the audit log history, an estimation can be provided for the trigger count.
